fulldatas.parties:
Syed Jaglul Hossain Pasha and others ----- Petitioners 
Vs.
Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents
fulldatas.full_judgment:
Mir Hashmat Ali J : All these Writ Petitions arise out of the property of the Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Mohammad Ahia Waqf Estate. As common question of facts and law are involved in these writ petitions they were heard together and are being disposed of by this common Judgment which will govern all the writ petitions. 

 5. In the year 1922 with the approval of the Assam Government KB Ahia Waqf Estate was established empowering the Government as trustee, As per terms and condition of Waqf deed the present Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet is the ex-officio Mutawalli. The said Waqf Estate is a Waqf-ul-Lillah. The said Kazir Bazar Hat was established in the year 1952 within the khas land of the said Waqf Estate and the Hat and Bazar take place in every Friday and Monday of the week. 

 7. Before expiry of said lease period, Mr Mokon Miah filed Title Suit No. 58 of 1970 for declaration of his statutory occupancy right and right of successive renewals of lease. The said suit was disposed of vide order dated 18-3-1974 on the terms of compromise and agreed upon that the lease period will continue. But the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet refused to accept rent from the said Mokon Miah. Consequently, the said Mokon Miah filed another Title Suit being Title Suit No. 306 of 1979 against the said KB Ahia Waqf Estate for declaration of permanent occupancy right of the said Hat and for permanent injunction restraining the KB Ahia Waqf Estate not to disturb the possession of the said Mokon Miah or evicting him from the said land (Hat) by force and also obtained an order of temporary injunction to that effect. The said order was upheld by the High Court Division as well as up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. 

 8. The said Mokon Miah adopted various devices for obtaining temporary injunction by filing suit and managed to keep the possession of the said Hat against the interest of the Waqf Estate. In this situation, the respondent No.3, Administrator of Waqf vide Memo No. 202 dated 24-6-1996 issued letter to the respondent No.6, the Divisional Commissioner stating that the KB Ahia Waqf Estate has been suffering from huge financial loss due to long pendency of Civil suits. Subsequently, on an application of the respondent No. 7, the said Kazir Bazar Hat was leased out in her favour in that view of the matter respondent No. 3 wrote a letter requesting the respondent No.6 to take necessary steps to execute a fresh lease deed in favour of respondent No.7 on the terms and conditions of the letter. As per the said letter of the respondent No. 3 a lease deed was prepared and vide Memo No. O:Pro:/Sylhet/ 823 dated 23-11-1997 the lease deed was approved. Accordingly the lease deed was executed in favour of respondent No. 7. It was stipulated in the said lease deed that the respondent No.7 would pay an amount of Taka 1,30,677.35 as premium for the lease period from 1977 to 1995 while she was in possession of the Kazir Bazar Hat. The lease was valued only Taka 9,500/- for the year 1997 by the respondent No. 6. The respondent No. 7 had given an undertaking to pay lease money since 1977 as per lease deed. Subsequently the lease of the said Kazir Bazar Hat was renewed in favour of the respondent No. 7 on 22 November, 2004 with an amount of Taka 1,000 for the year 2004-2005. 

 11. The further case of the petitioner is that Hat/Bazar situated within Sylhet City Corporation could not be legally owned and possessed by the respondent No. 6 due to whole sale acquisition of Khas land by the Government under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Hat and Bazar (Establishment and Management) Ordinance, 1959. The further case of the petitioner is that under section 2(12) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the cattle market is a "Hat" according to the definition of section 20(2a) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The land or structure therein of a Hat or Bazar has been excluded from retainable land and acquirable by the Government. sub-section 2(a) of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have retrospective effect of excluding Hat and Bazar from the category of retainable land and Hat and Bazar vested in the Government from the notification under section 3(2) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1956 and as such no fresh notification is required for inclusion of a Hat and Bazar. The further case of the petitioner is that section 20(5)(i)(c) excludes Waqf land from operation of sub-section (1), (2) and (3) of section 20, those subsections deal with retainable land. The provision of sub-section 6 of section 20 again excludes Hat or Bazar from the operation of sub section (c) of clause (i) of subsection (5) and Clause (ii) of that subsection i.e. Hat/Bazar are not retainable on the ground that those Hat and Bazar are Waqf Estate. 

 12. Further case of the petitioner is that Waqf Estate is not entitled to retain Hat /Bazar. Hat and Bazar land stands acquired on the date of notification under section 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. In the meantime, the Government has not taken over possession of the land of Waqf Estate having Hat and Bazar, the Mutawalli holding right title or any interest in the land having Hat/Bazar continued to manage as the agent of the Government till taking over possession. As per provision of the proviso (i) to section 10(a)(3)(b) no Mutawalli is competent to transfer or create any encumbrance or charge on any such interest over the said khas land in any manner except by a temporary lease not exceeding 1 year. Any transfer or any encumbrances or charge created or any lease given in contravention of the provision is null and void. The provision of section 39(1)(a) is clear with non-obstinate clause that land of Hat and Bazar under Waqf Estate is subject to acquisition and are entitled to compensation. The provision of section 2 of Hat and Bazar (State Acquisition) Ordinance 1959 provides establishment of any Hat and Bazar by any person other than the Government. The Local Administration may establish Hat and Bazar with the prior approval of the Government. Since notification under section 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has already been made. No fresh notification for Acquisition of Hat and Bazar of the Waqf Estate is necessary. Since there is no encumbrance in any manner in the Waqf Estate, even if there is any encumbrance in the property shall be null and void. The nullity of such encumbrance takes effect from the inception that means the encumbrance is void and ab initio. 

 13. Further case of the petitioner is that Kazir Bazar Hat managed by the Waqf Estate is situated within the Sylhet City Corporation is not retainable properly by the Waqf Estate. In view of clear provision of law, the Hat and Bazar is still retained by the Waqf Estate as their private property is wholly illegal and is being held in total violation of Provisions of law. The purported lease granted by the Waqf Authority as Waqf Estate from 1947 onward without any auction is in total violation of the provision of section 10(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. According to the provision of the said Act such continuance of lease without any auction is a nullity. 

 15. Mr Moudud Ahmed, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Dr AKM Ali with Mr Md Anowarul Islam for the petitioner submits that Kazir Bazar Hat is situated in the City of Sylhet. One KB Anis established a Waqf Estate in the year 1922 and Kazir Bazar Hat was established in 1952 one of the property of Waqf Estate. He further submitted that according to State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the Government acquired land and building of a Hat and Bazar including other thing under section 20(2a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Hat and Bazar (Establishment and Management Ordinance 1951) and, as such, the Kazir Bazar Hat is a Acquired property of the Government and that the said Hat should be leased out according to the guide line of Hat and Bazar vide Memo No. Proje e-/Ha-5/2000/408(5272) dated 20-7-2002 issued by the respondent No. 1 under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. But without complying the aforementioned guide line the said Hat and Bazar leased out by the respondent No. 6 in collaboration with respondent No. 7 with a nominal value. He further submitted that Hat and Bazar automatically vested to the Government by operation of law. He further submitted that the said Kazir Bazar Hat was established in the year 1952 within the land of the Waqf Estate which was given lease of the said Hat and Bazar by the Waqf Estate in the year 1354 BS to one Mokon Mia for a period of (six) years, which was continued until 1373 BS During the continuance of the said lease Mokon Miah filed Title Suit No. 58 of 1970 for declaration of his statutory occupancy right and right of successive renewals of the lease. The said suit was disposed of by an order dated 18-3-1974 on the terms of compromise, it was asserted that the lease will be continued. But subsequently the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet refused to accept rent from the said Mokon Miah. Consequently the said Mokon Miah filed Title Suit No. 306 of 1979 against the said Khan Bahadur Ahia Waqf Estate for declaration of permanent heritable lease and for permanent injunction restraining the authority from disturbing the possession of the said Mokon Miah or evicting him from the said premises. The said Mokon Miah obtained the order of temporary injunction against the eviction. The said order was also confirmed by the High Court Division as well as by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. 

 16. The said Mokon Miah adopted various devices for obtaining temporary injunction, managed to keep the possession of the said Hat and Bazar as against the interest of the Waqf Estate. Consequently, the respondent No. 3, Administrator of Waqf vide Memo No. 202 dated 24-6-1996 informed to the respondent No. 6 ex-officio Mutawalli that the suits are pending for a long period and the KB Ahia Waqf Estate has been suffering from financial loss. Subsequently the Waqf Authority without any public auction leased out the said Kazir Bazar Hat to Mrs Hamida Khatun daughter of Mokon Miah previous leasee. In that view of matter respondent No. 3 requested the respondent No. 6 to take necessary steps to execute a fresh lease deed in favour of respondent No. 7 on the terms and conditions as mentioned the said letter. 

 20. Mr TH Khan, the learned Senior Counsel appearing with Mr JN Deb and Mr Helaluddin Mollah and Mr AKM Shamsul Huq by filing affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit in opposition for the respondent Nos. 6 and 7 submitted that the property originally belonged to Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Mohammad Ahia who subsequently in the year 1922 established Waqf Estate as Waqf-ul-Lillah known as KB Ahia Waqf Estate under the approval of the then Government of Asham. Since then the case property along with other properties have been possessing and enjoying by the Waqf Estate. The Secretary, Ministry of Land, Respondent No. 2 also directed to the Deputy Commissioner of Sylhet, Maulvi Bazar, Sunamganj not to disturb the peaceful possession of the Waqf Estate and according to the said direction, the respondent No. 6 Waqf Estate filed Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 for correction of record which is still pending for determination and another Title Suit No.72 of 1999 in respect of permanent injunction was decreed in favour of the Waqf Estate against which no appeal was preferred. The petitioner has no locus standi to file instant writ petition. He further submitted that the property in question is Waqf ul Lillah and the income of the said Waqf-ul-Lillah being used for the benefit of charitable purpose. He further submitted that the whole sale acquisition under section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not applicable in respect of the properties under the Waqf Estate. Moreover, the Government did not acquired the property of the Waqf Estate till today nor the Government paid any compensation or award in favour of the Waqf authority till today nor there was any direction to handover possession of the Waqf Properties. He further submitted that the said Waqf Estate enrolled under Provisional Government of Asam which was subsequently, enrolled after partition of Bengal to the Waqf Administrator of East Pakistan under EC No. 13071 and before declaration of Sylhet Division, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet was the Mutawalli and after declaration of Division the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet became Mutawalli of the said Waqf Estate thus Managing the same, at the same time the Divisional Commissioner became the representative of the Government. Since at the time of SA operation some of the properties of the Waqf Estate was wrongly record in the name of Government as khas Land of the Government, Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet wrote a letter to the Secretary Ministry of Land, the Secretary, Ministry of Religious and the Deputy Commissioner of Sylhet to hold an enquiry and lastly the Divisional commissioner on 8-10-1987 issued a letter under Memo No. Vum-71/87/684 / (1) 4 stating that “এস্টেটের যে সকল সম্পত্তি ভুল ক্রমে সরকারী খাস খতিয়ান রেকর্ড করা হইয়াছে সেগুলি সংশোধনের ব্যবস্থা নিতে অনুরোধ জানাচ্ছে।” 

 21. Thereafter the Ministry of Land, respondent No. 2 vide Memo No. Vu:Ma: Sha/5/ Waqf/Sylhet/ 177/91(3) dated 5-8-1991 directed the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj, Habigonj, Moulvibazar not to interfere in the function of the Mutawalli of Khan Bahadur Waqf Estate in any manner and also to take proper steps for correction of wrong record. But inspite of the said memo, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet, Sunamganj and Moulvibazar trying to disturb the possession of the Waqf Estate. In such situation, one Shahid Mubarak instituted Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 before the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Sylhet praying for permanent injunction against the Deputy Commissioner, Habigonj, Sunamganj and Moulvibazar. After hearing of the suit, the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit against which no appeal has been preferred thus the said decree of permanent injunction is still in force. Another suit being Title Suit No. 07 of 2002 in respect of correction of wrong record is still pending before the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Habigonj. 

 22. The Government revenue head of Sylhet i.e. Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and after declaration of Sylhet Division the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet became Revenue head and Mutawalli and he has been managing and controlling and possessing all the Waqf Estate. He further submitted that from 1922 as per terms of registered Waqf Deed and as per approval of the then Asham provisional Government. By giving lease of the Waqf properties in favour of different persons including the present Kazir Bazar Hat and Bazar earning the money 100% of which is expending for the purpose of public interest and for the interest of other religious and charitable establishment. Since the property is the Waqf property, the Government has no jurisdiction to acquire the property of the Waqf Estate and that since the property is Waqf-ul-Lillah and as per section 20(5)(1(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the Kazir Bazar Hat was leased out on 15-12-2005 in favour of one Ms Hamida Khatun for the year 2006 only and the said leasee is in possession of the lease property. 

 23. He further submitted that the respondent No. 6 filed Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 before the Joint District Judge, Habigonj against the Government and others praying for declaration of Title in respect of the suit property including the land in question. The said Title Suit is still pending for final hearing. He further submitted that one of the leasee of the Government i.e. Md Shamsul Alam has filed writ petition No. 5164 of 2003 claiming some land of the Waqf Estate as the leasee of the Government. But the Rule was discharged with cost by the judgment and order dated 29-3-2005. Ministry of Land respondent No. 2 on 3-5-2006 wrote a letter to the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet by canceling their previous letter dated 1-1-2006 in respect of taking over possession of the case properties; which indicates that the property in question is a Waqf Property not Khas land of the Government. He further submitted that the property in question is the property of KB. Ahia Waqf Estate is 100% Waqf-ul-Lillah under section 20(5)(i)(c) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 100% Waqf-ul-Lillah property cannot be taken over by the Government. He further submitted that since there is a judgment and decree of permanent injunction against the Government in Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 in respect of the properties under the Waqf Estate, against which no appeal has been filed and as such the judgment and decree of the Title Suit No.72 of 1999 is binding upon the Government. Another Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 is still pending before the Second Court, Habigonj against the Government of Bangladesh in respect of the Waqf property prying for declaration of title and a such the instant writ petition is not maintainable. He further submitted that the property of the Waqf Estate is not normal. Hat and Bazar, it is the absolute property of the Waqf Estate and has been using for special purpose for cattle market for the people of the locality. Whether the property is normal Hat and Bazar under the definition of Hat, Bazar or not is a question of fact which can be decided in the civil Court not before this writ jurisdiction. 

 25. He further submitted that another Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 is still pending before the Court of Joint District Judge, Habigonj by Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Mohammad Ahia Waqf Estate represented by Ex-officio Mutawalli, the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet Division and the schedule of present writ petition is also subject-matter of the schedule of the said Title Suit No. 7 of 2002 and that the Title Suit is earlier then the instant writ petition, hence the judgment and decree has been passed in Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 and since no appeal has been preferred against said judgment and decree of the permanent injunction and if the civil Court pass a judgment and decree in that case on the same subject matter the result of the Rule of this writ petition may bring multiplicity of proceeding. 

 26. He further submitted that regarding the self same subject-matter of the writ petition, the predecessor of the respondent No. 7 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 363 of 1977 before the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet and vide order dated 8-11-1977 the said Court directed all the parties to maintain status quo. During the pendency of the said suit one Sirajul Islam filed an application for addition of party as co-plaintiff. Being unsuccessful, he filed civil revision No. 3789 of 1997 before the High Court and obtained an order of stay and also stay all further proceeding of the suit and the said civil revision is still pending and that the representative of KB Ahia Waqf Estate filed Title Suit No. 104 of 1997 before the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet which was eventually transferred to the Court of learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet and renumbered as Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 against the Government of Bangladesh, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and others and the said suit was decreed vide Judgment and decree dated 30-8-2001 by declaring that Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate is entitled to hold and possess the land of the Waqf Estate and also granted permanent injunction against the defendants restraining them from disturbing possession and management till preparation of the annuity and compensation assessment Role. Against the said judgment and decree none preferred any appeal and, as such, the said judgment and decree is still in force and binding upon the defendants. The Respondent No.6 also filed Title. Suit No. 7 of 2002 before the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court. Habigonj against the Government and others for declaration and for correction of record of right in respect of the subject-matter of this writ petition. The said Title Suit is still pending before the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Habigonj. 

 27. Md Mokon Miah the predecessor of the respondent No. 7 had filed Title Suit. No. 306 of 1979 before the Court of learned Munsif, Sadar, 1st Court, Sylhet which was eventually transferred to the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Biswanath, Sylhet and renumbered as Title Suit No. 82 of 1985 against the Waqf Estate and others for declaration of permanent heritable right of occupancy and in the alternation holding over tenancy right of the plaintiff and for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from disturbing the possession of the plaintiff in regard to the suit land or evicting him from the suit land by force except in due process of law. In the said suit, the Government official filed written statement stating cattle market is not retainable land. The prayer for temporary injunction was allowed by trial Court which was affirmed up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 366 of 1981 and the original suit is still pending before the trial Court for disposal. In the said suit one Sirajul Islam filed an application for adding as Co-plaintiff, which was rejected against which Sirajul Islam filed Civil Revision before this Court and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 4170 of 1996 which is still pending for disposal. 

 28. Mr MA Mannan the learned Advocate appearing for the Respondent No. 5 Sylhet City Corporation by submitting affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of the City Corporation stated that lease of cattle market in favour of Mokon Miah was granted by the Waqf Estate for 6(six) years and within his lease term he filed a suit for declaration of his occupancy right with a right of inheritance and for temporary injunction against the KB. Ahia Waqf Estate and being unsuccessful he fought up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court. Further stated that suit was ultimately compromised by the daughter of Mokon Miah Ms Hamida Khatun who filed case after case to keep the possession of the cattle market on frivolous and fraudulent steps. 

 29. Further stated that Mokon Miah adopted various tactics by filing suits for obtaining temporary injunction and to maintain possession of the cattle market against the interest of Waqf estate for which Waqf estate is suffering from financial loss. Further stated that deponent was not awarded any power according to letter of respondent No. 3 Further stated that the said Hat was illegally leased out to the respondent No. 7 and that Hat and Bazar automatically vested in the Government by operation of law. This deponent has no knowledge if the petitioner applied to the respondent No. 2 to take over possession of the Hat in question and to lease out the same as per guide line of the Hat and Bazar under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and that the respondent No. 6 illegally leased out the Hat in question and caused loss to the Government. 

 30. Mr Karuna Moy Chakma, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing with Enus Ali, the learned Assistant Attorney General by filing affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit-in-opposition on behalf of respondent No. 1 and 2 submitted that the Kazir Bazar cattle market is situated at the Northern side of East Kazir Bazar of Sylhet Town and it is the only cattle market in the Sylhet town. In the year 1922 with the approval of the Asham Government, Khan Bahadur Ahia established a Waqf Estate empowering the Government as trustee. As per term and condition of the Waqf deed the present Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet became ex-officio Mutawalli. The said Waqf Estate is called KB Ahia Waqfs estate. The Kazir Bazar Cattle market was established in the year 1952 in the land of the said Waqf Estate. Usually the said Hat sits on Monday and Friday of all the weeks and the said Kazir Bazar Hat was given lease to one Mokon Miah by the authority of the Waqf Estate in the year 1354 BS and at that time when the lease period has been expired the said Mokon Miah filed Title Suit No. 58 of 1977 for declaration of occupancy right successive renewal of lease. The said suit was disposed of on 18-34974. On the terms of compromise and it was stipulated in compromise that the lease would continue. But subsequently, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet refused to accept the said Mokon Miah as leasee. The said Mokon Miah then filed another suit being Title suit No. 145 of 1976 for specific performance of contract. Another suit being Title Suit No. 306 of 1979 was filed against KB Ahia Waqf Estate for declaration of permanent heritable or transferable right of occupancy of the said hat and obtained an ad-interim order of injunction against the Waqf Estate from evicting the plaintiff petitioner. The said ad-interim order of injunction was affirmed by the High Court Division as well by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. The said Mokon Miah adopted various devices by filing Title suit and obtained temporary injunction thus managed to keep the possession of the Hat against the interest of the Waqf Estate. Thereafter the Administrator of Waqf vide Memo No. 202 dated 24-6-1996 wrote a letter to the Divisional Commissioner and ex-officio Mutawalli stating that the Waqf Estate has been suffering from financial loss due to the long pendency of civil suits and these civil suits may take long time for final disposal. Subsequently due to the above reasoning the Waqf estate was leased out on the application of the respondent No. 7 Ms Hamida Khatun, the daughter of said Mokon Miah. Respondent No.3 requested the respondent No. 6 to take necessary steps to execute a lease deed in favour of respondent No. 7. The respondent No. 3 approved the deed of lease in favour of respondent No. 7 for the period of 1977 to 1995. Subsequently, the lease was granted for the year 2004-2005 fixing a lease amount of Tk. 1,00,000 The lease of the said Hat was granted by the Mutawalli of Khan Bahadur Waqf Estate but not according to the guide line of Hat and Bazar. 

 31. He further submitted that according to the decision of the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court reported in 28 DLR (AD) 195, property under Waqf-ul-Lillah cannot be acquired under section 20(5)(i)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and, as such, there is no question of taking over possession of the Waqf Estate by the respondents and that Kazir Bazar cattle market was established in 1952 and lease was granted on yearly basis according to the direction of the Waqf Administration and there is no order to hand over possession to the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet or Sylhet City Corporation and that the Ministry of Land directed the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet to correct the wrong recording of the Waqf Property vide Annexure-1 (A) which runs thus: 

 32. The petitioner in reply submits that ex-officio Mutawalli of Khan Bahadur Ahia Waqf Estate being public official cannot file any suit challenging the acquisition of property in question. Further submitted that the joint District judge, Habigonj has no jurisdiction to entertain any suit in respect of the property in question as it is beyond his territorial jurisdiction and that Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 the judgment and decree passed by the Court is contrary to the law under PO 19 of 1972 and that filing of a separate writ petition by one Shamsul Alam has got no relevancy with the instant writ petition. 

 34. The filing of the suits with all ulterior motive to continue illegal possession of the property in question, which stood acquired with the publication of the notice under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Any suit filed against the acquisition or any order passed by way of injunction to refrain the Government from taking possession in pursuance of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act abates under PO 19 of 1972. With the publication of the notification under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 all retainable interest including that of the Debutar and Waqf Estate stood acquired and all non retainable khas land also stood vested in the Government. Further stated that the letter dated 8-10-1989 (Annexure-2) and letter dated 5-8-1991 (Annexure-'3') are outcome of manipulation and connivance of some public official being gained over by the interested quarter to continue illegal possession of the cattle market and that no authority can pass any order to give any direction for Acquisition of the property which stood acquired and vested in the Government. The respondent No. 6 has no legal control or possession of the property in question. As per sub-section (2a) of section 20 any land or building in a Hat or Bazar vest to the Government with retrospective effect on the Publication of the notification under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1956, all rent receiving interest including that of Debattar and Waqf Estate stood acquired and all non-retainable khas land also vested in the Government and that the judgment and decree in question abated under PO 19 of 1972 and has no legal force. PO 19 of 1972 creates a complete bar to file a suit by any person or by entertaining any suit by any Court, challenging the validity and legality of any order of Acquisition taken or passed in pursuance of the acquisition under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 36. In writ petition No. 300 of 2006, the petitioner Most. Hamida Khatun challenged Memo No. Bhu. Mo /Sha-8/Khajab/745 /2005/ 02 dated 1-1-2006 issued under the signature of Senior Assistant Secretary of the Ministry of Land (Respondent No. 2) who directed the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet (Respondent No. 4) to take over possession of the Kazir Bazar Cattle Market and to hand over the same to the Sylhet City Corporation (Annexure-'H'). Further stated that the predecessor of the petitioner of writ petition No. 300 of 2006 filed Title Suit No. 363 of 1977 before the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet and vide order dated 8-11-1977 the trial Court directed the parties to maintain status quo over the cattle market. During the pendency of the said suit one Sirajul Islam filed application for addition of party. as co-plaintiff and on refusal by the trial Court he filed Civil Revision No. 3789 of 1997 before this Court and obtained Rule and an order of stay and also an order of stay all further proceeding of the suit. The said Civil Revision is still pending for disposal. The representatives of the KB Ahia Waqf Estate filed Title Suit No. 104 of 1997 against the Government, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and others before the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet which was eventually transferred to the Court of learned Subordinate judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet and renumbered as Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 and the same was decreed vide judgment and decree dated 30-8-2001 declaring that the Mutawalli is entitled to hold and possess the land of the Waqf Estate and also granted permanent injunction restraining the defendants from disturbing the possession and management' of the properties till preparation of annuity and compensation assessment role. Against which the defendants filed to appeal and 'the said judgment and decree is still in force. The petitioner of the writ petition No 300 of 2006 came to know of writ petition No. 9256 of 2005 (present writ petition) challenging the inaction of respondent No. 1, 2, 4 and 5 to take necessary steps to take over possession of the Hat and Bazar situated within the jurisdiction of the Sylhet City Corporation and to lease out the same in the Public auction as per guide line for Hat and Bazar. On the same day, the present petitioner came to know that vide Memo dated 1-1-2006 respondent No. 2, Senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Land directed the respondent No. 4, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet to take over possession of the Kazir Bazar cattle market and to hand over the same to the Sylhet City Corporation. Against the said order filed writ petition and obtained Rule and an order of status quo. The petitioner came to know of the same date, the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet wrote a letter to the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet requesting him to abide by the judgment and decree of the Civil Court and to refrain from disturbing the possession of the lessee. Further case of the petitioner is that under section 6(a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the petitioner is entitled to hold and possess the same and as such the impugned order dated 1-1-2006 has been passed without any lawful authority and is 'of no legal effect. 

 38. Further case that the predecessor of the petitioner Md Mokon Miah the previous lessee of Kazir Bazar Hat and at the request of the then Mutawalli of Khan Bahadur Ahia Waqf Estate Kazir Bazar cattle market was started with hard labour and by expending huge amount and also for the public purpose filed several suits before the Court of law to protect the Waqfs property from illegal activities and some of the suits are still pending for disposal with ad-interim order of injunction. The petitioner of the said writ petition No. 301 of 2006 is in peaceful possession of the Kazir Bazar cattle market and her right has also been protected by several suits against the Government and the Waqf Estate and the property in question is still the property of the Khan Bahadur Ehia Waqf Estate and till today no annuity of compensation assessment Roll has been prepared under the law and the same has been in possession of the petitioner. In view of the Waqf deed, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet was the official Mutawalli and after the declaration of Sylhet Division, the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet become the official Mutawalli and lease deeds was executed by the said official Mutawalli. The petitioner paid the lease money by Pay Order dated 11-12-2005 and the same has been accepted by the respondent No. 6 on 14-12-2005 and executed and registered the lease deed in favour of the petitioner for the year 2006. 

 40. The KB Ahia Waqf Estate filed Title Suit No. 104 of 1997 before the Second Court of learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet, which was eventually transferred to the Court of learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet and renumbered as Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 against the Government of Bangladesh, Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and others. The said suit was decreed vide judgment and decree dated 30-8-2001 by declaring that the Mutawalli is entitled to hold and possess the land of the Waqf Estate and also granted permanent injunction restraining the main defendants from disturbing possession and management of the property till preparation of the annuity and compensation assessment roll. Against the said judgment and decree none preferred any appeal and as such the said decree is still enforce and binding. 

 46. Md Abdul Hakim Mondal, the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet, Mutawalli of Khan Bahadur Ahia Waqf Estate represented by Md Abdur Rahman filed Writ Petition No. 331 of 2006 before this Court challenging the office Memo No. Vo:Ma/Sha-8/Kha:Ja:Ba:/745 /2005 /02 dated 1-1-2006 issued and signed by the respondent No. 5 Senior Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Land, section-8 stating that the properties in question known as Kazir Bazar Hat is situated under District-Sylhet, Upazilla-Sadar, Mouza-Sylhet Municipal area originally owned and possessed by Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Mohammad Ahia who established Waqf Estate on 16-2-1922 popularly known as KB Ahia Waqf Estate with other property including the present case properties. The said Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Mohammad Ahia executed and registered Waqf deed after obtained prior approval of the then Government of Asham and the terms and conditions as laid down in the said Registered Waqf deed the representative of the Government i.e. revenue head of Sylhet will be Mutawalli/Trustee of the said Waqf Estate and after partition of India, the said Waqf was enrolled as EC No. 13071 in the Office of the Waqf Administrator and before declaration of Sylhet Division, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet was the Mutawalli and after declaration of Sylhet Division as per terms of the deed, the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet being revenue head of Sylhet Division has became the Mutawalli of the said Waqf Estate and till today he is managing and controlling the properties of the said KB Ahia Waqf Estate. Before declaration of the Sylhet Division the property was managed and looked after by the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and the said Deputy Commissioner was the representative of the Government. Subsequently, some portion of the land of the Waqf Estate was wrongly recorded in SA Khatian as khas land and in respect of wrong recording the Secretary, Ministry of Land, the Secretary, Ministry of Religious and the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and Waqf Administrator made several correspondence letter to hold an enquiry and lastly on 8-10-1987 vide Memo No. Vum-71 /87/684/91) 4 issued by the Secretary Ministry of Land stated that- 

 47. Thereafter the Ministry of Land issued letter vide Memo No. Vu:Ma:Sha/5 /Waqf / Sylhet/177/91(3) dated 5-8-1991 directing the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj, Habigonj, Moulvibazar, Sylhet not to interfere in any manner of any activities of the Mutawalli of Khan Bahadur Ahia Waqf Estate till correction of wrong record. 

 48. In spite of the clear order of the Secretary, Ministry of Land directing the Deputy Commissioner, Habigonj, Sunamganj and Moulvibazar not to interfere with the activities of the Mutawalli in respect of the properties under KB Ahia Waqf Estate; the Deputy Commissioner, Habigonj, Sunamganj and Moulvibazar are trying to disturb the possession of the properties of Waqf Estate. In this situation one of the beneficiary of the said Waqf Estate namely Shahid Mubarak instituted Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 before the Court of learned Subordinate judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet praying for permanent injunction and after hearing all the parties, the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit. 

 49. Against the said judgment and decree no appeal has been preferred which is binding enforce. After declaration of the Sylhet Division, the Divisional Commissioner Sylhet as Mutawalli has been managing, controlling and possessing all the land of the Waqf Estate including the present case land and expending money for the public interest and in various religious, charitable organizations. 

 50. The KB Ahia Waqf Estate has been owning and possessing the case properties through different persons and since it is a Waqf-a-Lillah, 100% income of the aforesaid Waqf properties have been using for charitable purposes, under section 20 (5) (i) (e) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act-1950 has made it clear bar to acquire the properties of the Waqf Estate, therefore the Government has no jurisdiction to acquire the properties of the Waqf Estate. On 15-12-2005 the petitioner KB Ahia Waqf Estate made a lease deed of the case property in favour of the Ms Hamida Khatun for the year 2006. In this way the petitioner has been possessing and enjoying the case property of KB Ahia Waqf Estate. The respondent No. 6 with the intention of grabbing the properties of the Waqf Estate has filed suits and several applications and being unsuccessful on 14-12-2005 filed instant writ petition No. 9256 of 2005 and obtained Rule and also obtained an ad-interim order restraining the respondent No. 6 by an order of injunction from leasing out the said Kazir Bazar Hat in favour of Respondent No. 7. After obtaining the said Rule, the respondent No. 6 stated disturbing and trying to dispossessing the petitioner from the case properties and in one stage at the instigation of the said Respondent No. 6 the respondent No. 5 on behalf of the respondent No. 1 issued Memo No. Vo:Ma/Sha-8/Kha:Ja/Ba /745/ 2005/2002 dated 1-1-2006 stating that according to the direction of the High Court Division, the Government decided to take possession of Kazir Bazar Hat on 1-1-2006 and after taking possession, the hat will be leased out according to the policy of the management of Hat Bazar. According to the said policy they decided to hand over possession of the Hat in favour of Sylhet City Corporation. 

 52. The respondent No. 1 appeared and filed affidavit-in-opposition stating that Kazir Bazar Hat is situated at Mouza-Sylhet Municipality under Sylhet Sadar, District- Sylhet with an area of 1.553 acres which was owned by khan Bahadur Abu Naser Md Ahia. After obtaining approval from the then Government of Assam on 16th February, 1922, he made Waqf Eitate Known as KB Ahia Waqf Estate with the case properties along with other land measuring total area of 24,000 acre which was executed and registered on 16-2-1922. Afterwards the said Estate was enrolled as EC No. 13071. According to the terms of the said deed the representative of the Government revenue head i.e. the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet will act as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. After declaration of Sylhet Division, the Divisional Commissioner, Sylhet became a Mutawalli of the said Waqf Estate who is managing and controlling the said properties. Further stated that some of the land of the KB Ahia Waqf Estate was wrongly record in the name of the Government in Khatian No.1 as Khas land, Afterwards, the Ministry of land issued Memo dated 8-10-1987 for correction of record and also memo No. Vu;Ma:/Sha/5/ Waqf/Sylhet/ 177/91 (3) dated 5-8-1991. But the Deputy Commissioner, Habigonj, Sunamganj and Moulvibazar tried to disturb the properties of the Waqf Estate. As a result, one of the beneficiary of the Waqf Estate Shahid Mubarak instituted Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 before the Court of learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet. The said suit was decreed with permanent injunction but no appeal has been preferred against the said decree. The petitioner has been possessing the properties and spending the income accumulated from the properties in various charitable purposes. The Waqf Estates are not acquirable by the Government as per section 20(5)(4)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and as such the petitioner executed a lease deed of the properties as mentioned and possessing the same. 

 53. The respondent No. 4, Sylhet City Corporation appeared and filed affidavit-in-opposition denying the assertion that Shahid Mubarak instituted Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 and obtained decree for permanent injunction and that the said decree is still in force. Further denying that the petitioner has been owning and possessing by giving lease in favour of different persons or that 100% income of the Waqf Properties have been using for charitable purpose or that the Government has no jurisdiction to acquire the properties of the Waqf Estate. 

 58. The Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 filed by one Shahid Mubarak, a beneficiary of KB Ahia Waqf Estate is contrary to the clear provision of PO 90 of 1972 and, as such, decree has no legal force. Further stated that the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Habigonj has no territorial jurisdiction to entertain any suit against the Deputy Commissioner of Sylhet, Sunamganj and Moulvibazar. The so called decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge automatically abates in view of PO. 90 of 1972. The Courts are in complete bar to entertain any suit by any person challenging the legality or validity of the acquisition or any order passed in pursuance of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and that the Divisional Commissioner (Writ Petitioner) Ex-officio Mutawalli has no legal authority to manage and control the property already vested in the. Government by operation of law and that all the rent receiving interest including the properties of the Waqf Estate and Debuttor vested in the Government. The retrospective amendment made by Ordinance No. XII of 1960 in section 20 by the incorporation of sub-section (2a) which has effect of excluding hats and bazars in the khas possession of the rent receivers became vested in the Government from the date of notification in 1956 under sub-section 2(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 63. In the instant case, the petitioner claims to have been aggrieved by the lease of Kazir Bazar Cattle Market by the Mutawalli of KB Ahia Waqf Estate, which appears to us that the petitioner personally aggrieved not for the common purpose of the country as a whole. 

 64. Next question is that, whether Kazir Bazar Cattle Market is a property under the KB Ahia Waqf Estate or acquired under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 65. It appears that one Khan Bahadur Ahia executed a Waqf deed in the year 1922 with the approval of Asham Government measuring an area of 24,000 acres of land including the land situated in Kazir Bazar. Kazir Bazar Cattle Market has been established in the land of KB Ahia Waqf Estate and that Kazir. Bazar Cattle Market takes place every Friday and Monday of each week. The petitioner himself also admitted that Kazir Bazar Cattle Market situated in Plot No. 1354 measuring an area of 1.555 acres under Sylhet - Municipality a property of KB Ahia Waqf estate. The said Cattle Market was given lease to one Mokon Miah by the Mutawalli of KB Ahia Waqf Estate in the years 1354 BS for a period of 6 (six) years which continued till 1373 BS. 

 66. It further appears that the Mutawalli of KB Ehia Waqf Estate, Divisional Commissioner leased out the said Cattle Market in the year 2006, it was leased out to one Ms Hamida Khatun daughter of Late Mokon Miah. Though there are suits between the parties, which are not relevant and not necessary to discuss in the instant writ petition. 

 67. Let us see, as to whether the said Kazir Bazar Cattle Market is retainable under the law. Though Title Suit No. 72 of 1999 filed by one of the beneficiary (Shahid Mubarak) of KB Ehia Waqf Estate who obtained a decree of permanent injunction from the civil Court in respect of schedule property of the suit, against which no appeal has been preferred by any quarter. As per section 20 (5) (i) (c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the 100%. Waqf-a-Lillah property cannot be taken over by the Government. Those properties cannot be dealt with under section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 69. In view of the provision Of Section 10A the Government cannot take over possession of the property-of the Waqf-Estate from which income  is being used for the purpose of charitable organization. 

 70. In the instant case, Chief Revenue Officer of the Division is the Mutawalli of the KB Ahia Waqf Estate and admittedly the Mutawalli is in possession through lease and has been  treating as an agent of the Government as contemplated under section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Which has been settled in the case of Bangladesh vs Dewan Anwar Raja Chowdluiry, being dead his heirs; Dewan Shamsul Abedin reported  in BCR 1984 (AD) 231. 

 73. In the instant case, there is no publication of compensation assessment roll under section 43 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act The, respondent No. 1 and 2 in their affidavit in opposition as well as supplementary affidavit in opposition has categorically admitted that no compensation assessment role has been prepared and published according to the provision of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and Rules there under and as such we find that the property in question is still the property of the KB Ahia Waqf Estate and it will remains so until the Government takes steps in accordance with law. 

 74. Let us see whether the petitioner can agitate the matter regarding the property of the Waqf Estates, let us see Article 102 of our Constitution, the relevant portion of which reads as follows : 

 75. In the instant case, the petitioner has prayed a direction to take over possession of the Kazir Bazar Hat and also challenged the lease of the Kazir Bazar Cattle Market made by Mutawalli of KB Ahia Waqf Estate. We have already held that the property in question is the property under Waqf Estate (waqfs-a-lillah) not yet acquisitioned and no compensation assessment Role was prepared no the property vested to the Government and that the Mutawalli of the KB Ahia Waqf Estate is not performing any function in connection with affairs of the republic but in the capacity of the terms of the Waqf deed of Khan Bahadur Abu Naser Md Ahia Waqf Estate (commonly known as KB Ahia Waqf Estate) and as such we do not find any ground to pass any order upon the respondent No. 6. 

 76. The respondent No. 1 and 2 in their affidavit-in-opposition admitted that the property relates to the property of the Waqf Estate and as such we also do not find any ground to make any direction upon the Respondents No. 1 and 2 to take any steps until and unless the property vest upon the Republic in accordance with law.

fulldatas.full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique, J: This appeal has arisen out of the leave granted on 14.03.2011 in Civil Review Petition No.90 of 2010 directed against the judgment and order dated 06.05.2010 passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1359 of 2009 affirming the judgment and decree dated 13.05.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.181 of 2004 affirming those dated 13.05.2008 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.59 of 1994. 

 3. The relevant facts, for the disposal of this appeal, are that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 herein as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.59 of 1994 and Money Suit No.2 of 2002 in the Second Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Title Suit No.59 of 1994 was for declaration of their title to the suit land; recovery of khas possession; for further declaration that the plaintiffs are not bound by the judgment and decree dated 15.11.1979 passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 by the Subordinate Judge, third Court, Dhaka; also for declaration that the kabala executed through Court on 27.02.1980 in execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 is fraudulent, collusive, illegal and void and same is not binding upon the plaintiffs and for permanent injunction. 

 4. Their specific case, in short, was that the land measuring an area of .0568 acre appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.241, C.S. Plot No.390/3940, S.A. Khatian No.197, S.A. Plot No.555, R.S. Khatian No.1511, 1522 and R.S. Plot No.1263 of Lalbag Mouza, Touzi No.61/1, Ward No.7, Sheet No.10, District-Dhaka, as described in the schedule to the plaint originally belonged to Khiroda Shundari Daishya. The suit property was sold in auction for arrear of rent in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 and the same was purchased by Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Monjurul Hoque on 20.06.1953. The sale was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and the sale certificate was issued on 19.11.1953. Possession of the suit land was delivered on 20.01.1954 to the auction purchaser. Ali Ahmed got his name mutated in the Khatian and paid rent to the Government. S.A. Khatian No.197 and R.S. Khatian No.1248 were prepared in his name. He died on 18.06.1975 leaving behind a widow, namely, Khatibunnessa, who inherited the entire suit property as his heir and as per provision of the 'Doctrine of Return'. Khatibunnessa died on 10.02.1978 leaving her only brother Abdul Mannan, who inherited her entire property including the suit property. He transferred the suit property to the plaintiffs by a registered heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 29.11.1979. Thus, the plaintiffs became owners of the suit property. The defendants forged some papers and tried to take over possession of the suit property forcibly but due to intervention of the respectable people of the locality, they could not take over possession of the same. On 06.07.1980, the defendants along with a process server of the Court and police tried to take over the possession of suit property again but the plaintiffs, by showing decree of the court, resisted them. After holding inquiry from the bailiff of the Court, the plaintiffs' father, Abdul Majid, came to know that the defendants had obtained a fraudulent decree on 15.11.1979 in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 from the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on the basis of an agreement dated 12.06.1972 executed by Rasheda Begum. Rasheda Begum had no title and possession in the suit land and, therefore, the defendants did not acquire any title on the basis of the decree. The defendants got a kabala deed executed and registered in their names through Court in execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979. Neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor were made parties in the said suit. Therefore, the decree passed in the said suit is not binding upon them. The plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.329 of 1980 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka against the defendants for permanent injunction, which was decreed on 28.03.1984 on contest. Against which, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No.196 of 1984 and, on transfer, the same was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.2, Dhaka, who allowed the appeal on 24.01.1987 and dismissed the suit. The plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No.76 of 1987 in the High Court Division but the rule was discharged on 27.05.1992. Then the plaintiffs filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.297 of 1992 in the Appellate Division, and the same was also dismissed. On 27.10.1993, the plaintiffs filed an application under Order XXI rule 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure for dismissing the Title Execution Case No.3 of 1980, arising out of the decree passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 which was rejected on 29.01.1994. Though the defendants failed to dispossess the plaintiffs, they declared that they would soon dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit property. The cause of action of the suit arose on 21.10.1993 when the defendants along with the bailiff of the Court asked the plaintiffs to hand over vacant possession of the suit property to them. When the suit was at the stage of peremptory hearing, the defendants along with 20/25 terrorists being armed with dangerous weapons, entered into the suit property forcibly on 16.09.1997 and evicted the plaintiffs and their men therefrom. They looted away the household articles worth of Tk.6,00,000/-, and also looted the goods of his tenants of the suit premises and took over possession of the same. The defendants deprived the plaintiffs from getting rent of their tenants. After that incident, Abdul Majid, the father of the plaintiffs, lodged a First Information Report with Lalbagh Police Station under Section 144/447/448 and 380 of the Penal Code. On behalf of the tenants, one Wazir Ahmed also lodged an FIR with the said police station which was registered as Lalbagh P.S. Case No.940 dated 16/09/1997. Thereafter, the defendants, by making threat to the plaintiffs and their father Abdul Majid, took signature in a white paper and prepared a money receipt of 16,60,000/-. The defendants demolished the one storied building and the shop rooms situated in the suit land causing a loss of taka 20 lacs to the plaintiffs. So, they are entitled to get mesne profit. In the premises, the plaintiffs filed Money Suit No.2 of 2002 claiming Tk.28,71,900/- with interest and cost. 

 5. The defendant-appellants contested the suits by filing written statements. Their case, in short, was that the suit property of No.1 Atash Khana Lane, along with other property owned by Khiroda Shundari Daishya. Khiroda sold the entire suit property to Salimunnesa by a registered kabala dated 27/03/1953 and delivered possession. Salimunnesa transferred her 8(eight) annas share to Rasheda Begum and the rest 8(eight) annas to Mohammad Ilias on 15/06/1959, Ilias, by a registered deed of gift, transferred his said 8 (eight) annas share to Rasheda Begum and delivered possession. Thus, Rasheda Begum became 16 (sixteen) annas owner and possessor of the suit property. One Munjurul Hoq was tenant in a portion of the suit property. He defaulted to pay rent. Accordingly, Rasheda filed Money Suit No.50 of 1959 in the 3rd Court of the then Munsif, Dhaka for the realization of arrear rent. Rasheda Begum also filed House Rent Case No.598 of 1959 for eviction of Dr. Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed. The tenant, forging signatures of Rasheda Begum, filed two applications for compromise in the name of Rasheda Begum and Khatimunnesa respectively in the said money suit and House Rent case and obtained compromise decrees. Knowing about the same, Rasheda Begum filed Title Suit No.221 of 1964 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka praying for cancellation of the deeds of agreement dated 16/11/1959 as well compromise petitions filed in Money Suit No.50 of 1959 and House Rent Case No.598 of 1959 and for setting aside those fraudulent compromise decrees. Section 4 of the Public Demand and Recovery Act (PDR Act)prescribes the mode of filing of certificate for Public demand payable to the Collector and directs that when the certificate officer is satisfied that any public demand payable to the Collector is due, he may sign a certificate in the prescribed form stating that the demand is due. Section 5 provides that when any public demand payable to any person other than the Collector is due such person may send written requisition in the prescribed form to the certificate officer. Section 6 of the PDR Act provides that on receipt of such requisition the certificate officer, if lie is satisfied that the demand is recoverable and that recovery is not barred by law, may sign a certificate in the prescribed form stating that the demand is due. Section 7 provides that when a certificate has been filed in the office of the certificate officer under section 4 or 6, he shall cause to be served upon the certificate debtor in the prescribed manner a notice in the prescribed form and a copy of the certificate. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that certificate holder R.L. Govt. Acquired Estate had any demand (Public demand?) chargeable from the certificate debtors Khiroda Sundari Saha and Lalit Mohan Saha(?) for which, it made requisition to the Certificate Officer of 'Das Group Govt.-Ad Estate' who issued notice in Form 2 of schedule II and being satisfied that the demand was chargeable or became due so he signed the certificate.

'Public demand' means any arrear or money mentioned or referred to in schedule-1, i and includes any interest which may, by law, be chargeable thereon up to the date on which a certificate is signed under part II of the PDR Act. It is to be mentioned here that as per provision Section 3(3) of the PDR Act "Certificate Officer" means a collector and any officer, appointed by a Collector to perform the functions of a Certificate Officer under the Act. The Court of Wards can send requisition under section 5 of the PDR Act but requirement is that on receipt of a requisition filed under section 5 the Certificate Officer before signing a certificate must be satisfied, far as the demand made in the requisition is concerned, that it is recoverable. There is no evidence that Deputy Collector appointed any one/officer of Das Group Govt. AD Estate as Certificate Officer.

 20. Another aspect is that it is well settled that the certificate of sale does not, by itself, create the title but is merely evidence of title. In the case of Ahmedabad Municipality Vs. Hazi Abdul reported in AIR 1971 SC 1201 it was observed by the Supreme Court of India that it is axiomatic that the purchaser at auction sale takes the property subject to all the defects of title and the doctrine caveat emptor (let the purchaser beware) applies to such purchaser. It is the "right, title and interest" of the judgment-debtor with all risk and defect and without any warranty of title either by the decree-holder or by the court that passes to a purchaser at a court sale, with the exception that where it is proved that the judgment-debtor had no saleable interest at all the purchaser may recover back the purchase-money. In this case, the alleged auction was held on 20.06.1953 showing Khiroda Sundari Saha and Lalit Mohon Saha as certificate debtors. But we have already found from C.S. Khatian (ext-1) shows that Khiroda Sundari Dashya was only C.S. recorded tenant and before holding auction she sold her rayoti interest to Salimunnessa on 27.03.1953 who was not impleaded in the certificate procedure. That is, Khiroda had no right and title at the time of holding auction in suit property so the auction purchaser had not acquired any title because, at the time of holding auction the certificate debtor had no title in the property, in question. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that Salimunnessa had notice of the alleged charges brought by R.L. Acquired Government Estate either actual or constructive. It is to be relevant here to reiterating that in Title Suit No.221 of 1964, the learned Munsif observed that Khiroda and Lalit Mohon were the certificate debtors who already sold their interest to Salimunessa with the knowledge of the defendant No.1, that is, predecessor of the present plaintiffs. Lalit Mohan and Khiroda had no subsisting interest on the date of holding auction sale and it cannot be said that the defendant No.1 (predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs) acquired 7 annas interest by his purchase in the certificate sale. That judgment was upheld in Second Appeal No. 1095 of 1966. That finding is binding upon the plaintiffs. The effect of a sale under the PDR Act being to pass to the purchaser merely the right, title and interest of the person named as judgment debtor in the certificate, the purchaser acquires no right if the person appears to have i no interest in the property at the date of sale. That is, auction purchaser Ali Ahmed did not get any title under it. In Title Suit No.221 of 1964, Title Appeal No.50 1966 and Second Appeal No.1 095 of 1966, the respective Courts had taken notice of the same. But the plaintiffs did not meet up the issue raised and explain the consequences of the same.
