The defendants by putting threat on the life of the plaintiffs as well as their father Abdul Majid also got a blank paper signed by them with the writing to the effect "16,60,000/- টাকা বুঝিয়া পাইলাম” although, they have not received any money from the defendants. The defendants demolished the entire one storied building and the shop rooms standing on the suit property causing a loss of taka 20 lacs to the plaintiffs. Therefore, the plaintiffs after their eviction prayed for restoration of possession to the suit property. They also filed Money Suit No. 02 of 2002 for Tk. 28,71,000/- as mesne profit. 

 29. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 (herein appellants) contested the suit by filing written statements admitting that Khiroda Shundari Daishya was the sixteen annas owner of the suit property. However, according to them, while Khiroda Shundari Daishya had been in possession of the suit property she sold the suit property to one Salimunnesa by a registered kabala being, No. 2042 dated 27.03.1953 and delivered possession thereof to her. Salimunnesa while had been in possession of the suit property, transferred her eight annas share to Rasheda Begum and the rest eight annas share to Mohammad Ilias on 15.06.1959. Mohammad Ilias by a registered deed of gift transferred his eight annas share to Rasheda Begum and delivered possession of the same to her. Thus, Rasheda Begum became 16(sixteen) annas owner of the suit property, Rasheda Begum had been in possession of the suit property by mutating her name. One Munjurul Hoq was a tenant in a portion of the suit property and he defaulted in paying monthly rents. So, Rasheda Begum filed Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka for realization of the arrear rents. Rasheda Begum also filed House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 for evicting her tenant Doctor Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed. But Ali Ahmed created two forged registered deeds of agreement on 16.11.1959 being deed No. 6904 and 6905 by forging the signatures of Rasheda Begum. On the same date, Manjurul Haque also procured two applications for compromise of the aforesaid money suit and the house rent control case in the name of Rasheda Begum and Khatumunnesa through forgery and under duress. In the compromise agreements Doctor Manjurul Haque claimed that he purchased 7(seven) annas share of the suit plot in the auction held on 18.06.1953. Whereupon, Rasheda Begum filed Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka praying for cancellation of said agreements dated 16.11.1959 and also for cancellation of the applications for compromise filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Control Case No. 598 of 1959. In the said suit these defendants claimed that Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Dash sold the suit property to Salimunnesa on 27.05.1954 and that Khatimunnesa, wife of Doctor Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed was a tenant under Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Dash and that after transfer of the suit property she become a tenant under Salimunnesa. Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 was decreed on 25.12.1965 in favour of Rasheda Begum declaring the registered agreements being Nos. 6904 and 6905 dated on 16.11.1959 as cancelled and ineffective. The trial Court further declared the compromise applications filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Control Case No. 598 of 1959 as cancelled. Doctor Manjurul Haque and Khatimunnesa than filed Title Appeal No. 50 of 1966 before the District Judge, Dhaka and the appeal was heard by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and was dismissed. Thereafter, Majurul Haque and his wife filed Second Appeal No. 1095 of 1966 before the High court Division but the said appeal was dismissed. Then the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 in the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title to the suit land and also for declaration that the plaintiffs are not bound by the judgment and decree dated 15.11.1979 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979. The plaintiff also filed Money Suit No.73 of 2000 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for realization of compensation of taka 28,71,900/-(twenty eight lacs seventy one thousand and nine hundred) along with interest @ of 15% till realization, and the Money Suit was transferred to the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and renumbered as Money Suit No. 2 of 2002. Both the suits were tried simultaneously and decreed in favour of plaintiffs, respondents herein. Thereafter, the defendants as appellants filed First Appeal No. 181 of 2004 before the High Court Division and the High Court Division by judgment dated 13 day of May, 2008 dismissed the appeals and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Whereupon, the present appellants filed CPLA. No. 1358-1359 of 2009 before this Division and this Division by order dated 13.05.2008 dismissed CPLA No. 1358 of 2009 arising out of Money Suit No. 02 of 2002 and LA No. 1359 of 2009 arising out of Title Suit No. 59 of 1994. Then the present appellants, who were defendants of the aforesaid suits filed Civil Review Petition No. 90 of 2010 before this Division. 

 "I. Whether the Gazette notification dated 2nd April 1956 No 4024 LR(sic No.4824 LR) and No.  4836 LR respectively under section 3 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (Act XXVIII of 1951) (hereinafter mentioned as the SA&T Act) as amended by E.P. Ordinance III of 1956, the rent receiving interest vested in the Government on 02.04. I 956 and exhibit-1 shows Khiroda Shundari Daishya held a Mirash Ijara  interest wider a private land lord and it conclusively proves that the certificate case No. 660 of 1952-53 issued by L.R. Government Acquired Estate are manufactured papers and exhibits-2 and 2(ka) are all also forged papers and the claim of title of the plaintiffs falls through. 

 II. Whether the finding that the certificate was filed by the Government for arrears of rent in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 while the exhibits 2 and 2(ka) show that certificate was filed by R.L. Government Acquired Estate against the provision of section 4 of Public Demand Recovery Act, 1913 (hereinafter referred to as the PDR Act) is a mistake apparent on the face of record and in the circumstances, judgment dated 06.05.2010 calls for review." 

 (1) Admittedly, Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohon Dash were original tenants of the suit property under a private zamindar (জমিদার) i.e. landlord Lakshmi Narayan and others as per Exhibit- 1 i.e. C.S. Khatian. (2) The root of plaintiffs case is that their predecessor in interest Ali Ahmed Dr. Monjurul Haque had purchased the suit property in auction from the R.L. Government Acquired Estates in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 through exhibit 2 and got possession thereof from the said estate through exhibit 2(ka). 

 (3) Gazette notification was published on 14 April, 1956 being notification No. LR 4826, LR 4836 acquiring the rent receiving interest by the Government and, as such, there was neither any scope of auction sell nor to deliver possession of the suit property by R.L. Government Acquired Estate in Auction by exhibits 2 and 2(ka). 

 (7) Lalit Mohan and Khiroda Shundari Daishya sold the suit property to Salimunnasa on 27.05.1954 and the Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 was filed by R.L. Government Acquired Estate under the PDR Act for arrear of rents, when the Government had no rent receiving interest. 

 (IV) the appellants suppressed the fact that their predecessor-in-interest Mohammad Joynal Abedin, father of appellant No. 1 had entered into an agreement to purchase the adjacent land to the suit property from one Piru Sardar @ Piru Miah under a registered agreement of sale executed on 24 July, 1964 and the said Joynal Abedin also purchased the same by registered conveyance deeds No. 3775 and 3776 for the year 1965 and that the adjacent land of the suit property was also auction purchased by Abdul Hug son of Lutfur Rahman from R.L. (Rup Lal) Government Acquired Estates in auction. So, the appellants cannot claim that the property could not have been sold in auction in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53. 

 (VI) the appellants' predecessor in interest Mohammad Ilyas had also taken lease in terms of registered deed of lease No. 3022 dated 16.06.1954 from Golam Mohammad who had purchased the same in Certificate Case No. 659 of 1952-53 of the Certificate Officer at 74, Bashanta Kumar Road, Dhaka and the Certificate Case was filed by the R.L. Government Acquired Estate and none else under the law. 

 (VII) the aforementioned registered deed of lease dated 16.06.1954 in the name of Mohammad Ilyas (predecessor in interest of the appellants) shows that the certificate case was filed by R.L. Government Acquired Estate, obviously under section 4 read with section 3(3) of the PDR Act. 

 (IX) the plaintiff-respondents have not been able to search out Extra-ordinary Gazette Notification, dated Wednesday March 19, 1952 bearing No. 2906 L.R-28th February, 1952 by which Ruplal Wards Estate was acquired by the Government under section 3(1) of the SA&T Act). But from Extra-ordinary Gazette Notification dated February 12, 1954 bearing No. 1815 L.R. 6th February, 1954 it appears that reference has been given about acquisition of Rup Lal Wards Estate on 28.02.1952 under section 3(1) of the SA&T Act by Gazette Notification dated 19.03.1952. 

 (XI) R.L.(Rup Lal) Estate was owner of 7 annas share of Tauzi No. 61/1 (Part of Touzi No. 61) of Dhaka Collectorate and being Wards Estate it was being managed by the Government under the Court of Wards Act as prevalent. Therefore, by Notification No. 2906 L.R. dated 28.02.1952 as mentioned in the Gazette Notification No. 1815 L.R. dated 6111 February 1954, the Government got ownership of R.L. Estate. 

 (XII) the Government in order to realize the arrear rents of R.L.( Rup Lal) Court of Wards Estate from defaulter tenant Khiroda Shundari Daishya of C.S. Holding (Milts) No. 241 of Plot No. 390/3940 of the said Tauzi No. 61/1 filed Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 under section 62 read with section 139 and section 141 of SA&T Act against Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Dash and the suit property was sold in auction to Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Monjurul Hoque on 20.06.1953. Said auction was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and he got delivery of possession of the suit property measuring .568 ajutangsha on 20.01.1954 vide exhibits 2 and 2(ka). 

 (XIII)some other lands of Tauzi No. 61/1 of R.L. Estate were also sold in auction mentioning its 7 annas share of the said Tauzi on the same day (2.0.06.1953) vide Certificate Case No. 659 of 1952-53 and one Golam Mohammad purchased the land of Holding No. 246 in auction and got deliver y of possession on 28.04.1954. The said Golam Mohammad transferred the said land to Mohammad Iliyas, vide Deed of Lease in Perpetuity No. 3022 dated 16.06.1954 and the defendants eventually purchased the same. 

 (XIV) likewise some land of Holding No. 236 of R.L. Estate was also sold in Certificate Case No. 657 of 1952-53 of Tauzi No. 61/1 mentioning its 7 annas share and Golam Mohammad also purchased the same in auction. Thereafter, Golam Mohammad transferred the said plots to Mst. Habiban Nesa wife of Piru Sardar alias Piru Mia vide sale Deed No. 3827 dated 03.09.1954. The defendant - appellants subsequently purchased it. (XV) it is evident from exhibit 2 and 2(ka), deed of lease in perpetuity bein2 No. 1022 dated 16.06.1954 and sale deed No. 3827 and 03.09.1954 that R.L. Government Acquired Estate was the owner of 7 annas share of Tauzi No. 61/1, and it was the rent receiver. (XVI)Therefore, the Government being in management of R.L. Estate on 28.02.1952 legally sold the suit property to the plaintiffs' predecessor in interest in auction. All the alleged predecessor-in-interest of the defendants were never in possession of the suit property by their so called forged/fraudulent deeds of purchase at any time. Similarly, the defendants never dot possession of the suit property in due process of law at any time but they forcibly evicted the plaintiffs during pendency of the suit. 

 34. We have examined the judgment of the trial Court dated 31.03.2004 passed in Title Suit No. 59 of 1994, the judgment and decree dated 12th and 13th day of May, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 181 of 2004, the judgment and order dated 06.05.2010 passed by the Appellate Division in CPLA No. 1359 of 2009, sale Certificate No. 660 of 1952-53 (exhibit-2), certificate of delivery of possession (exhibit-2(ka), Dhaka Gazette Extra-ordinary published by the authority on April 2, 1956, Gazette Extra-ordinary dated 12.02.1954 and the judgment and decree passed by various Courts in various suits, appeals, etc. and the connected materials on record. 

 37. From the exhibit-1, copy of C.S. Khatian, it appears that Zamindar Lakshmi Narayan and others were seven annas owners of Tauzi No. 61 which includes Tauzi No. 61/1, Khatian No. 241 of Mouza-Sahar, Dhaka, Police Station-Kotwali and Khiroda Shundari Daishya was in possession of No. 1, Atash Khana Lane as a tenant of Zamindar Lakshmi Narayan and others. Exhibit 1 has not been challenged by the defendants side. 

 38. The ground taken in this appeal are that admittedly Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohon Das were tenants under private landlord and so, the sale certificate in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 issued by R.L. Government Acquired Estate and the writ of delivery of possession are manufactured documents as the rent receiving interest vested to the Government in the year, 1956 according to Gazette dated 02.04.1956. Thus, both exhibits 2 and 2(ka) are forged documents. 

 41. On careful scrutiny of the sale certificate of Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 (exhibit-2) it is found that both the stamps of sale certificate were purchased immediately before the date of issuance of sale certificate. Moreover, it appears that by the said sale certificate the certificate officer sold .568 ajutangsha of property of C.S. 390 Khatian No. 241 and C.S. plot No. 390/3940 Atash Khana, Ward No. 7, Sheet No. 10 under Lalbagh Police Station, Sahar Dhaka, Touzi No. 61/1 of the Collectorate of Zilla Dhaka. 

 42. We are of the considered opinion that R.L. (Rup Lal) Court of Wards Estate was the owner of 7 annas share of Tauzi No. 61/1, which is a part of original Tauzi No. 61, of Sahar Dhaka of the Collectorate of Zilla-Dacca. It transpires from the C.S Khatian that it is written therein that Khiroda Shundari Daishya was in possession of No. 1, Atash Khana Lane of Mouza Sahar Dhaka of Khatian No. 241. This clearly shows that the words "Sahar Dhaka" as used in the auction sale certificate was the Mouza of the property sold in auction and the word “মৌজে আতস খানা” does not mean Mouza but it was the lane i.e. Mash Khana Lane. Further, from the deed of sale (Exbt-Ka) submitted by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 (appellants) it appears that the Police Station of the suit property has been stated therein as Kotwali at Present P.S.- Lalbag being premises No. 1, Atash Khana Lane, Dhaka. Thus it is evident that C.S. Khatian No. 241 was originally under P.S. Kotwali but subsequently it fell within P.S. Lalbag. Further, we searched the Gazette of establishment of Lalbag Police Station and finally it was found from the Culcutta Gazette, September 22, 19 45 that: 

 44. So, it appears that P.S. Lalbag was also correctly mentioned in the sale certificate. Therefore, R.L Estate was the owner of 7 annas share of the aforesaid Tauzi and .568 ajutangsha out of the said 7 annas was sold in auction from khatian No: 241 in favour of Ali Ahmed son of Late Munshi Nawab Jan on 20.06.1953. From the writ of delivery of possession (Exhibit 2(Ka) it appears that possession of the aforesaid land was delivered to Ali Ahmed. Relevant part of this document reads as under: 

 103. Babu Jagesh Chandra Das, son of Radhaballav Das, Babu Tarak Nath Das, son of Ramesh Chandra Das, of Farashganj, Dacca, (Wards, Ruplal Wards Estate, Dacca).	2906 L.R. dated 28.2.1952, under section 3(1). 

 48. Whereas the gazette notification dated 02.04.1956 as referred to by Mr. Quiyum reads as under: "No. 4836 L.R. — 2nd April 1956. — In exercise of the power conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (East Bengal Act No. XXVIII of 1951), as amended by the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (East Bengal Ordinance No. III of 1956), it is hereby notified, for the information of all concerned, that the governor is leased to acquire, with effect from the 14th April 1956, all interests of all rent-receivers in their respective estates taluks, tenures, holdings and tenancies situated in the district of Dacca, including their interests in all sub-soil and rights to minerals in such estates, taluks, tenures, holdings and tenancies, except the interests and rights which have already been acquired by, and have already vested in, the Provincial Government under the provisions of the said Act." 

 49. Thus, Gazette notification dated 02 April, 1956 excludes the property of Rup Lal Acquired Estate as it was acquired earlier in 2906 LR dated 28.02.1952, published in Dhaka Gazette Extra-ordinary dated 19.03.1952, as apparent from Colum 03 of Gazette Notification dated February 12, 1954. 

 50. Therefore, it appears from the Dhaka Gazette Extra-ordinary published by the authority on February 12, 1954 that the Governor was pleased to order preparation of compensation of assessment roll of the properties which were acquired under section 3(1) of the SA&T Act by notification referred to in Colum 03. It further appears that Rup Lal Wards Estate, Dacca was acquired in 2906 L.R. dated 28.02.1952, under section 3(1) of the SA&T Act and it was notified in the Gazette on 19.03.1952. 

 51. In view of the above, it is evident that the entire R.L. (Rup Lal) Wards Estate, whether be it Tauzi No. 61 or 61/1, was under the management of the Government at the relevant time as a Wards Estate prior to 19.03.1952. Therefore, it appears that even prior to acquisition of rent receiving interest by the Government, it had the right to auction sale the suit property for arrear rents of Rup Lal Court of Wards Estate. 

 53. However, in the Gazette notification it is mentioned that the properties of Jogesh Chandra Das, son of Radhaballab Das, Babu Tarak Nath Das, son of Ramesh Chandra Das of Farashganj, Dacca were being managed by Wards, Rup Lal Wards Estate, Dacca. 

 54. None of the parties could explain about the Rup Lal Court of Wards Estate's ownership of the property but this Gazette Notification was never challenged by the defendants. Thus, the Government being in management of RL Wards Estate had lawfully auction sold the suit property of Wards Estate in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 and so, it cannot be said that the certificate of auction sale Exhibit- 2 is a forged document. 

 62. Further, from the materials on rerecord it appears that some other lands of Tauzi Nos. 61 and 61/1 of R.L. Ward Estate were also sold in auction by mentioning its 7 annas share of the said Tauzi on the same day, i.e. on 20.06.1953 vide Certificate Case No. 659 of 1952-53 and one Golam Mohammad purchased land of Holding No. 246 in auction and got delivery of possession on 28.04.1954. The said Golam Mohammad transferred the said land to Mohammad Iliyas, vide Deed of Lease in Perpetuity No. 3022 dated 16.06.1954. Land of Holding .No. 236 of R.L. Estate was also sold in Certificate Case No. 657 of 1952-53 of Tauzi No. 61/1 mentioning its 7 annas share and Golam Mohammad also purchased the same in auction. Thereafter, Golam Mohammad transferred the said plots to Mst. Habiban Nesa wife of Piru Sardar alias Piru Mia, vide sale Deed No. 3827 dated 03.09.1954. So, it is evident that some other lands of Tauzi No. 61/1 were also sold in auction by R.L. Ward Estate, in certificate cases of 1952-53 of R.L. Acquired Estate. 

 73. We have already seen that in fact the Rup Lal Government Acquired Estate was the owner of 7 annas share of the Tauzi and out of it .568 ajutangsha of land was sold in auction. Moreover, the plaintiffs were admittedly in possession of the suit property. Therefore, if any one claims title to or ownership of the same or part of it, they shall have to file a suit for declaration of title, partition and possession. The defendants, under no circumstance were entitled to evict the plaintiffs from the suit property.

fulldatas.full_judgment:
The Rule issued in this Civil Revision is about sustainability of the judgment and decree dated 27-05-2007 by which the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka dismissed Title Appeal No. 174 of 1998 and thereby affirmed those dated 16-04-1998 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 2nd Additional Court, Dhaka dismissing Title Suit No. 84 of 1997 instituted for declaration of title to 25 1/2 decimals of land and for recovery of khas possession thereof. 

 After the death of Abdul Gafur, his four sons being plaintiff’s grandfather Nowab Mia, Abed Mia, Yousuf Mia, Yukub Mia and the children of a pre-deceassion son Sona Mia used to possess the land of the entire jote. The three daughters of Gafur never possessed or claimed their shares in the suit holding. 

 Accordingly the S.A record was prepared in the names of the said 4(four) sons and grandchildren of Abdul Gafur. There was an amicable partition among the S.A. recorded tenants. The suit plot No. 181 fell in the share of two brothers Nowab and Yusuf who used to possess the eastern 18 decimals and the western 18 decimals respectively. 

 Out of that western 18 decimals Nowab Mia, by registered deed of exchange of 1962, transferred a small portion measuring 26 cubit × 5 cubit i.e. about 3/4 (three fourth) decimal to a neighbor named Maleka Bibi so that she could use that portion as an exit path to the neighboring road from her homestead on the contiguous plot No. 180. In the exchange deed, Maleka specifically admitted that Nowab Mia was in possession of the contiguous eastern side of the path i.e. the western part of the suit plot No.181 accordingly Maleka and her son Asadullah Master used that path. 

 The predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-12 being Sowdagor used to live at a distance of about 300 yards from plot No. 180. He wanted to shift his house on plot No.180. So Sawdagar and the said Maleka and her son Asadullah executed an exchange deed in 1963 and thus Sawdagar got from Maleka and others plot no 180 and the said path. In this exchange deed, Sawdagor also admitted the aforesaid possession of Nowab. Subsequently Sawdagar’s son Ala Uddin (defendant No.2) purchased some land in the non-disputed contiguous plot Nos. 185 and 186 and constructed a house on those two plots and also on plot No. 180 and all the defendants have been using the said exit path. 

 Nowab Mia’s brother Yousuf sold his share i.e. the remaining eastern 18 cents of the suit plot by a kabala dated 09-04-1963 to one Ibrahim who sold the same to one Awalad @ Awal by kabala dated 02-07-1963. Later on this Awlad @ Awal sold the same to Nowab Mia by Kabala dated 16-03-1981. 

 Thus Nowab Mia acquired a total of 17.25+18 = 35’25 decimals of the suit plot by way of inheritance-cum-amicable partition and purchase. During his exclusive possession, Nowab Mia sold 16 decimals out of that land to his grand son being the plaintiff by kabala dated 14-01-1985. By a subsequent deed of Hiba-bil-Ewaz dated 03-10-1988 Nowab Mia transferred the remaining 19 decimals to the plaintiff and defendant No. 13 being a son of Nowab Mia. Thus plaintiff acquired the suit land measuring 25 1/2 decimals in the suit plot. 

 However, at one stage, Nowab Mia’s two brothers Yousuf and Yakub started demanding some land in the suit plot although they had no subsisting interest. So plaintiff’s grand father Nowab Mia, to avoid future complication obtained kabala dated 19-07-1988 executed by the said Yousuf and Yakub in the benami of the plaintiff and defendant No.13. 

 However they admit that the suit plot originally belonged to Asak Ullah and that he died leaving one son Abdul Gafur and three daughters being Rahela and two others. They have not denied the existence of Nawab, Yusuf and others as the children of Gafur and also the standing of plaintiff as the grand son of Nowab. 

 It is noted that the appellate court recorded a finding that Nowab (plaintiff’s grandfather) and his brother were in possession but did not record any finding as to when and how the defendants took over possession from Nowab and his brothers. 

 Mr. Bhuyian, the learned advocate, next submits that the appellate court failed to consider the exact quantum of plaintiff’s claim as stated in the schedule and in para 9 and 10 of the plaint wherein the plaintiff has specifically stated that he is entitled to 25 1/2 decimals and not the entire plot measuring 35 decimals and that the remaining 9 1/2 decimals was acquired by defendant No.13, being son of Nowab Ali. 

 (2)	Exhibts-3 and 4, being the two exchange deeds of 1962 and 1963, prove that Sawdagar the father of defendant No. 1 and 2 and Sadagar’s predecessor-in-interest Maleka had admitted the possession of Nowab over the western part of the suit plot. 

 (3)	Exhibit-14, being the kabala dated 28-01-1979, proves that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 they and their brother Askar, being predecessor of defendant Nos. 3-12 admitted the possession of Nowab over the western part of the suit plot. 

 (4)	Exhibit-5-7 being the various kabalas that led to the purchase of eastern 18 decimals of the suit plot by Nowab from the sucessors-in-interest of his brother Yusuf. 

 (5)	The R.S. khatian No. 86 (admitted in evidence in appeal) and the mutation khatian No.1 23/1 (Exhibit-8) were solely prepared only in the name of Nowab pursuant to the above purchases and these documents prove the exclusive possession of Nowab. 

 (6)	Exhibits-9 and 10 prove acquisition of the suit land measuring 25 1/2 decimals by plaintiff from Nowab and Exhibt-11(series) being the D.C.R. and Rent receipt prove the mutation obtained and rent paid by the plaintiff. 

 (10)	In line with D.W.2 and 3, Hashem P.W.4 stated that plaintiff and his grandfather Nowab used to grow IRRI paddy on the suit land before dispossession by the defendants. 

 Mr. Bhuiyan next submits that since the defendants themselves and their father Sawdagar and their predecessor-in-interest Maleka admitted possession of Nowab, being the plaintiff’s grandfather-and-predecessor-in-interest, the defendants are estopped from denying such possession as enunciated in the case of Bazlur Rahuman and others vs. Sadu Mia others (45 DLR (1983-page-391). 

 The R.S record khatian No.86, admitted as evidence in appeal but not marked as Exhibit, shows that it was prepared only in the name of Nowab. This document also does not prove the fact of oral gift as alleged by the plaintiff. 

 But the entries in these documents are partly correct and do not establish exclusive title of plaintiff’s predecessor Nowab Mia or of the latter’s brother Yusuf and others in the present scenario. Simply because the original owner and C.S. tenant Asakullah admittedly died leaving one son Gafur and three daughter’s including Rahela and there is no reliable evidence that these daughters or their heirs lost their interest. 

 On the other hand, the defendants in their written statements have not denied the status of Nawab Mia as the son of Gafur being the admitted son of the C.S tenant Asakullah. Moreover the S.A. and R.S. record show that Nowab was one of the sons of Gafur. 

 The sale deeds (Exhibits-5-7) show that Yousuf being another son of Gafur transferred his interest in the suit plot to one Ibrahim leading to the purchase thereof by Nowab. 

 (1)	Exhibt-3, the registered exchange deed dated 03-03-1962 shows that one Maleka acquired from plaintiff’s grandfather Nowab Ali a path measuring 26 cubits × 5 cubits in the western part of the suit plot No.181 and she admitted that Nawab was in possession of the eastern side of the path i.e. the western part of the suit plot. 

 The above mentioned three documents clearly prove that the defendants themselves and their predecessor Sawdagor admitted possession of Nowab in the eastern part of the suit plot during the period from 1962 to 1979. 

 Accordingly I hold that the defendants are estopped form denying possession of Nowab. This finding is supported by the principle laid down in the case of Bazlur Rahman and others vs. Sadu Mia and others (45 DLR(1983) page-391, para-5, as follows (underlines added): 

 The description of the land transferred by the aforementioned three documents (Exhibits- 3, 4 and 14) show that the location of plot Nos. 180 and 185 is to the north of the suit plot No.181 and that Nowab was in possession of the western part of the suit plot No.181. 

 Exclusive possession of Nowab is further supported by the R.S. record and mutation khatian Exhibit-8. 

 D.W.2, aged 55, categorically stated in cross-examination that defendants possess the suit land by raising a tinshsed on part of the suit land since one or two years before 1988 and that defendants cultivate vegetable on the remaining part and that before such cultivation, the plaintiff Atar Ali and his grandfather Nowab used to grow IRRI paddy on the suit land. 

 P.W.3, son of Abed being son of Gafur Munshi son of Asakullah, stated that his two paternal uncles, Yusuf and Nowab used to possess the suit plot by “informal partition” and that later on Yusuf sold his share to Ibrahim and that finally Nowab purchased it and plaintiff acquired the suit land form Nowab but dispossessed by the defendants in the later part of 1988. 

 Thus the material documentary and oral evidence as discussed above lead me to conclude that plaintiff’s grandfather Nowab was in possession of the western 17.25 decimals (other than the exit path) upto 1981 and then he acquired the remaining 18 decimals of the eastern part from the successor-in-interest of his brother Yusuf and after Nowab, the plaintiff acquired possession of the suit land by virtue of the transfer deeds of 1985 and 1988 (Exhibit-9 and 10). 

 It is noted that Exhibit-12 being the kabala dated 12-07-1988 shows that Yusuf and Yakub, the two brothers of Nowab, purportedly transferred the entire suit plot to plaintiff and his paternal uncle (defendant No.13). On the basis of this document, the appellate court recorded a finding that Yusuf and Yakub were in possession. 

 There is nothing record to show that Yusuf, after the said transfer in 1963, continued possession in any portion of the plot or that the other brother Yakub ever possessed any portion of the plot. In fact, possession of Yakub is no body’s case, rather the defendants deny the possession of all the children of Gafur i.e. Yusuf, Yakub, Nowab etc. 

 I have found that, plaintiff’s predecessor Nowab was a co-sharer in possession since at least 1962 and after him plaintiff has been a co-sharer since 1985 and plaintiff had been in possession of the suit land before his dispossession in 1988. So, plaintiff’s possession was the continuation of the possession of his predecessor that was admitted by the defendants in 1979 and also by their predecessors in 1962 and 1963. No doubt plaintiff has a right to continue it, and therefore he is entitled to recovery of possession under section-8 as quoted above. 

 a)	The judgment and order dated 27-05-2007 (decree signed on 30-06-2007) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 84 of 1997 is hereby set aside. 

 b)	Judgment and order dated 16-04-1998 (decree signed on 23-04-1988) passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 84 of 1997 is also set aside.

fulldatas.lawyer:
Mostafa Niaz Mohammad with Muntasir Uddin Ahmed, Advocates-----For the Petitioner 
Majumder Saiful Islam, Advocate-----For the Respondent No.4
fulldatas.parties:
Idris Chowdhury (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs
Waqfs Administrator Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents
fulldatas.full_judgment:
Moyeenul Islam Chowdhury J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order of appointment of Md Shah Alam alias Md Shah Alam Chowdhury as Official Mutawalli of Md Taqui Chowdhury Waqf Estate under section 44 of the Waqfs Ordinance, 1962 issued by the Waqfs Administrator, Bangladesh under Memo No. O. Pro./Cha./ Uo./170/09 dated 10-8-2009 (Annexure-'D') should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 On 22-11-1901 the grandfather of the petitioner late Sheikh Ahmad Ali Chowdhury dedicated some of his properties for creation of Md Taqui Chowdhury Mosque Estate (EC No. 1155) by a Waqf-al-Awlad deed. According to the terms of the Waqf deed, the descendants of the wakif's family became the Mutawallis of the Waqf Estate one by one. In this way, the Waqf Estate was successfully managed and administered by the heirs of the wakif. The last Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate was Md Ali Chowdhury of the same family. While he was managing the affairs of the Waqf Estate as Mutawalli, he died on 17-4-2007. After the death of Md Ali Chowdhury, the petitioner, being the proper descendant in order as per the deed of Waqf, started performing the functions of the Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate unofficially. While the petitioner was managing and administering the Waqf Estate as its Mutawalli unofficially and contemplating to make an application to the Waqf Administrator of Bangladesh to become Mutawalli as per terms of the Waqf deed, one Md Shah Alam (respondent No.4) made an application to the Waqf Administrator to become Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate on 12-4-2009. However, the petitioner made an application to the Waqf Administrator for his appointment as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate on 30-7-2009. But curiously enough, the Waqf Administrator did not respond to his application dated 30-7-2009 and appointed the respondent No.4 Md Shah Alam as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate by the impugned order dated 10-8-2009 on the basis of a report of the Waqf Inspector of Chittagong. Anyway, the respondent No. 4 Md Shah Alam is a stranger to the Waqf Estate. He has no interest whatsoever therein. According to the deed of Waqf, the Waqf is for the benefit of the local mosque and the descendants of the wakif. Besides, the mode of appointment of Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate is stated in the deed of Waqf. As a lineal descendant of the wakif, the petitioner is eminently suitable for the office of Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. Against this backdrop, the application by a third party (respondent No. 4) for appointment of Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate in the name of alleged mismanagement thereof cannot be entertained. So the appointment of the respondent No. 4 as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate cannot be sustained in law. Although the application of the petitioner dated 30-7-2009 was pending for disposal before the Waqf Administrator, the petitioner was not given any opportunity of being heard and behind his back, the impugned order dated 10-8-2009 was passed. 

 As per desire of the local people and to save the Waqf Estate from extinction, the respondent No. 4 made an application to the Waqf Administrator to appoint him as Mutawalli of the same. On receipt of the application filed by the respondent No. 4, the Waqf Administrator caused an inquiry into the affairs of the Waqf Estate by a Waqf Inspector of Chittagong. According to the report of the Waqf Inspector, the allegations leveled against the descendants of the wakif were prima facie proved and accordingly the Waqf Inspector recommended to appoint the respondent no.4 as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. On the basis of the recommendation made by the Waqf Inspector, the respondent No.4 was appointed as Official Mutawalli. 

 4. Be that as it may, the petitioner himself, amongst others was present at the time of holding of the inquiry by the Waqf Inspector. In reality, the inquiry was carried out in his very presence. Although the respondent No. 4 is not a descendant of the wakif but he is very devout Muslim. Out of his concern for protection of the Waqf Estate from extinction, he made .an application to the Waqf Administrator for his appointment as Official Mutawalli. It is a fact that the petitioner is a descendant of the wakif, but he is not a competent person to be appointed as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. The petitioner and other descendants of the wakif executed a bainapatra for selling of a portion of the Waqf property in favour of a third party. So in the hands of the petitioner and other descendants of the wakif, the Waqf Estate is not safe. 

 5. In the Supplementary Affidavit-in-Opposition dated 19-5-2010, it has been averred that the petitioner was away from the country for many years and on his return from abroad, he took over as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate unofficially but he did not make any application for appointment as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate in accordance with the terms and conditions of the deed of Waqf. Due to chaos, mismanagement and irregularity in the affairs of the Waqf Estate, the Waqf Administrator appointed the respondent No. 4 as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate legally and validly. 

 7. In the Affidavit-in-Reply dated 7-6-2010, it has been mentioned that the property referred to in the bainapatra is vague and nebulous. Moreover, the alleged bainapatra has not been acted upon and no sale deed has been executed in favour of Zafar Ahmed. The payment of Taka 2,850 by way of subscription to the office of the Waqf Administrator by the respondent No. 4 prior to his appointment as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate is indicative of his mala fide intention. The respondent No. 4 has no right to meddle into the affairs of the Waqf Estate which was created for the benefit and welfare of the descendants of the wakif. 

 8. At the outset, Mr. Mostafa Niaz Mohammad, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits' that admittedly the wakif Sheikh Ahmed Ali Chowdhury created the Waqf-Al-Awlad, namely, Md Taqui Choudhury Waqf Estate on 22-11-1901 and in the Waqf deed, there is clear mode of appointment of Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate from amongst the descendants of the wakif and the petitioner, being admittedly a descendant of the wakif, has the indefeasible right to be appointed as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate in terms of the Waqf deed; but the sudden appointment of the respondent No.4 as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate under section 44 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 runs counter to the stipulation of the deed of Waqf in that regard and that being so, the impugned order dated 10-8-2009 is without lawful authority. 

 9. Mr Mostafa Niaz Mohammad further submits that it is an indisputable fact that the respondent No.4 is a stranger and is not related to the family of the wakif and since he is a busybody, his appointment as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate is unlawful. 

 10. Mr Mostafa Niaz Mohammad next submits that admittedly the last Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate Md Ali Chowdhury died on 17-4-2007 and thereafter for about two years, the petitioner failed to make any application to the Waqf Administrator formally for his appointment as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate in accordance with the terms and conditions of the Waqf deed, but the fact remains that he managed the affairs thereof unofficially during the interregnum. 

 12. Mr Mostafa Niaz Mohammad further submits that by way of making the application dated 30-7-2009 to the Waqf Administrator for his appointment as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate, the petitioner invoked Section 51 of the Waqf Ordinance and since no rival claimant was found among the descendants of the wakif, the delay of about 2(two) years in the matter of invocation of Section 51 of the Ordinance will not be fatal to the merit of the case. 

 15. Mr Majumder Saiful Islam also submits that the power of the Waqf Administrator to appoint an Official Mutawalli under Section 44 of the Ordinance, through unfettered, yet he assigned a reason in the impugned order for appointment of the respondent No.4 as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate and that being so, it is very difficult to find fault therewith. 

 16. Mr Majumder Saiful Islam further submits that after the death of the last Mutawalli on 17-4-2007, the Waqf Estate was virtually left uncared for bordering on extinction and given this panorama, the respondent No. 4 made an application to the Waqf Administrator on 12-4-2009 for his appointment as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate and after causing an inquiry into the allegations raised by the respondent No. 4, the Waqf Administrator was satisfied as to the veracity of those allegations and ultimately he passed the impugned order dated 10-8-2009 on the basis of the recommendation made by the Waqf Inspector contained in his report dated 3-8-2009 and such being the state of affairs, no exception can be taken to the impugned appointment of the respondent No. 4 as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. 

 17. Mr Majumder Safiul Islam next submits that it is true that the respondent No. 4 is not a kith of the wakif's family; but that does not pose as an impediment to his appointment as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate under Section 44 of the Ordinance and by that reason, he was appointed as Official Mutawalli by the Waqf Administrator to save it from extinction. 

 18. Majumder Saiful Islam also submits that the respondent no. 4 is "any other person" adverted to in section 51 of the Ordinance and after a long lapse of about 2(two) years from the date of death of the last Mutawalli, he had to invoke the provisions of section 51 under compelling circumstances and being left with no other option and the Waqf Administrator, relying on the report of the Waqf Inspector, appointed him as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. 

 19. Mr Majumder Saiful Islam next submits that since immediate action was necessary to save the Waqf Estate from Extinction, the Waqf Administrator had to pass the impugned order without hearing the petitioner in person and as this is an exceptional circumstance, the non-adherence to the principle of "Audi Alteram Partem" will not vitiate the impugned order dated 108-2009. 

 22. It is an admitted fact that Md Taqui Chowdhury Waqf Estate was found on 22-12-1901 by the wakif Sheikh Ahmed Ali Chowdhury and the character of the Waqf is Waqf-al-Awlad. As per the stipulations embodied in the deed of Waqf, the first Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate was Mr Abdul Majid Chowdhury, a son of wakif. The second Mutawalli of the Estate was Mr Golam Rabbani Chowdhury and the third Mutawalli was Golam Sobhan Chowdhury, sons of the wakif. The 4th Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate was Md Ali Chowdhury, a son of Golam Rabbani Chowdhury and a grand-son of the Wakif Sheikh Ahmed Ali Chowdhury who died on 17-4-2007. 

 23. It is also admitted that after the death of the last Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate on 17-4-2007, the petitioner, or for that matter, any other descendant of the wakif did not make any application to the Waqf Administrator for appointment as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate for about 2(two) years. Presumably finding no other alternative, the respondent No.4 Mr Shah Alam, though an outsider, made an application to the Waqf Administrator on 12-4-2009 (Annexure-'B') for his appointment as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate. The record shows that after filing of the application by the respondent No. 4 on 12-4-2009, the petitioner made an application dated 30-7-2009 (Annexure-'C') to the Waqf Administrator for his appointment as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate in terms of the Waqf deed. So the factual position is that without any justifiable reason, the petitioner slept over the matter and purportedly managed the affairs of the Waqf Estate unofficially during the interregnum. In the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the filing of the application dated 30-7-2009 to the Waqf Administrator by the petitioner is an after-thought. This conduct of the petitioner is deprecated. 

 25. Undeniably, the petitioner being a prospective Mutawalli did not notify the change in the management of the Waqf Estate to the Administrator of Waqf due to the death of the last Mutawalli Md Ali Chowdhury forthwith as mandated by section 51 of the Ordinance. Anyway, in the facts and circumstances of the case, we are at one with the contention of Mr Majumder Safiul Islam that the respondent No. 4 falls within the ambit of the phrase "any other person" referred to in section 51 of the Ordinance. In such a situation, it cannot be said that the respondent No.4 is a busybody. So we opine that he rightly and legally made the application dated 12-4-2009 to the Waqf Administrator, having regard to section 51 of the Ordinance. 

 27. Now let us scan the impugned order dated 10-8-2009. From a bare reading of the same, it seems that in the interest of proper management of the administration of the Waqf Estate, the respondent No.4 was appointed as Official Mutawalli. It also appears that at the time of passing of the Impugned order dated 10-8-2009 by the Waqf Administrator, the application dated 30-7-2009 filed by the petitioner for his appointment as Mutawalli in terms of the Waqf deed was very much before him, but he passed the impugned order without giving him any opportunity of being heard. Mr Mostafa Niaz Mohammad has emphatically contended that the impugned order is without lawful authority in view of non-adherence to the principle of "Audi Alteram Partem" In this connection, the contention of Mr Majumder Saiful Islam is that since the petitioner was physically present at the time of inquiry held by the Waqf Inspector, the principle of natural justice was substantially complied with before passing of the impugned order. But it should be borne in mind that the Waqf Inspector is not the decision making authority. He was just entrusted with the duty of holding of the inquiry into the allegations leveled against the descendants of the wakif. As per the relevant provisions of the Waqf Ordinance, the decision making authority is the Waqf Administrator. Had the Waqf Administrator afforded the petitioner an opportunity of being heard before issuance of the impugned order, probably the petitioner would have no legs to stand upon. 

 34. Reverting to the case in hand, the impugned order of the Waqfs Administrator has affected the complaining party, that is to say, the petitioner. From this point of view, it was incumbent upon the Waqf Administrator to adhere to the principle of 'Audi Alteram Partem" before issuance of the impugned order affecting his right or interest in relation to the Waqf Estate due to the admitted position that he is a descendant of the wakif. 

 35. From the foregoing discussions and in the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears to us that no opportunity was afforded to the petitioner to controvert the allegations leveled against him and other descendants of the wakif's family. As a matter of fact, the petitioner did not have a fair deal before the Waqf Administrator especially when his application for appointment as Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate was pending before the Waqf Administrator prior to issuance of the impugned order. As admittedly the petitioner was condemned unheard, the impugned order, as we see it, is without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 36. In our view, the power vested by section 44 of the Waqf Ordinance in the Waqf Administrator is an extra-ordinary power and this power should be exercised by him sparingly 'where considered necessary' by adherence to the principle of "Audi Alteram Partem". In the instant case, this having not been done, the impugned order appointing the respondent No. 4 as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate is a nullity in the eye of law. 

 Accordingly, the Rue is made absolute without any order as to costs. The Impugned appointment of the respondent No. 4 Md Shah Alam @ Md Saha Alam Chowdhury as Official Mutawalli of the Waqf Estate under section 44 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 issued by the Waqf Administrator under Memo No. O. Pro./Cha. Uo/170/09 dated 10-8-2009 (Annexure-'D') is declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect. However, the Waqf Administrator will be at liberty to hear the parties concerned and give a decision afresh with regard to appointment of the Mutawalli of the Waqf State in accordance with law.

fulldatas.parties:
Nawab Khaja Habibullah Askari & others ------ Petitioners 
Vs
Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
fulldatas.full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: This Rule has been obtained upon an application filed under Article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh calling upon the respondents Nos.1-5 to show cause as to why they should not be directed to release the Estate of late Nawab of Dhaka Khaja Salimullah Bahadur from the custody of Court of Wards in favour of the petitioners (4 in all) and respondent Nos. 6-8, 10-34, 36-39 and 41-47. 

 2. In support of the prayer of having the properties, as claimed to have been of late Nowab of Dhaka Khaja Salimullah, released from the custody of Court of Wards petitioners have stated, inter alia, that said Nowab mortgaged some properties to Raja Sreenath Roy and others of Bhaggapur and also to Raja Sreenath Roy; that the mortgage suit Nos. 12 of 1907 and 16 of 1907 were instituted by the mortgagees in the Court of First Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and they obtained decree therein; that the Nowab having found himself in a precarious financial predicament to satisfy the mortgage decrees applied for a loan of Taka 14 lakh to the Government of India, that the Secretary of State for India considered the application of the Nawab in council and communicated Government of India's decision to grant loan against the security of the movable and immovable properties of Nowab, that a mortgage deed was drawn and executed on 6th August, 1908 between the Court of Wards 1st Part and the Nowab in the second part and the Secretary of State for India in the third part; that by the aforesaid mortgage deed movable and immovable properties described in the schedule to the mortgage deed were mortgaged for satisfaction of debt of Taka 14 lakh out of which Taka 3,11,500 was paid by the Collector of Dhaka as purchase money together with incidental cost for repayment and purchase of mortgage decrees of Raja Sreenath Roy and others and adjusted, as such, against the said loan; that mortgage deed provided for repayment of debt with interest at the stipulated rate within 30 years by the Court of Wards. It was further stipulated in the mortgage deed, that neither the said ward nor his heirs, successors, executors, administrator and assigns shall be able to take back any of the property mortgaged from the custody of the Court of Wards as long as the whole amount of mortgaged money is not repaid; that 30 years period expired on 6-7-1938 and thereafter, another 57 years passed from August, 1938 but the property is still retained by the Court of Wards. It has been alleged that the Court of Wards did not furnish any statement of accounts of the repayment of debt either to the Nawab or to any of his heirs or successors and, as such, the petitioners and the respondent Nos. 6-8, 10-34, 36-39 and 41-47 are quite in the dark about the matter of repayment of loan. It has been contended by the petitioners that they have reasonable cause to believe that out of the income of the mortgage property the loan of Taka 14 lakh had already been paid and the Court of Wards has been arbitrarily and illegally continuing the possession of the property mortgaged by the mortgage deed dated 6th August, 1908. 

 3. Respondent Nos. 2 and 5—The Chairman, Land Reform Board and the Chief Manager of Court of Wards—respectively have entered appearances and have filed affidavit-in-opposition. These respondents upon denying the correctness of the material averments made in the writ petition have stated, inter alia, that the title i.e. Nowab, is not an inheritable one and that the claim of the petitioners as of being Nawab is unfounded and unsustainable one; that the claim of the petitioners that they and respondents Nos. 6-8, 10-34, 36-39 and 41-47, hereinafter referred to as said respondents, are the present sole exclusive heirs/successors is not correct, that neither the petitioners nor the said respondents had established their claim of inheritance and succession by any cogent evidence before the Court of Wards; that the petitioners nor the said respondents have filed any papers showing that they are the sole proprietor of the property which was placed under the management of the Court of Wards; that almost 50% of the wards of the original owner had left Bangladesh and that their whereabouts were not known, as such, their property has assumed the character of abandoned property and that vested in the Government as per provision of President's Order No.16 of 1972; that the said respondents have not filed any paper before the Court of Wards in support of their claim of being proprietor of the property managed by the Court of Wards, nor they have approached the Court of Wards seeking release of the property from the management thereof, that joint proprietorship has not been partitioned and, as such, the Court of Wards in the absence of determination of share of the petitioners as well as the said respondents and other proprietors of the property, in law, cannot release the property to the petitioners and the said respondents, that the petitioners have not made any statement as to how the mortgaged properties were redeemed and discharged from the mortgage debt, nor the petitioners have given any particulars and description of the property which was the subject matter of the mortgage; that it is not correct that the Court of Wards did not furnish any statement of account of repayment of debt either to the Nowab Khaja Salimullah Bahadur or to any of his heirs or successors, or it is correct that the petitioners and the said respondents were ignored about the matter; that the petitioners' contention of repayment of loan out of income of the mortgaged property and that even after repayment and disbursement of amount for which the property was mortgaged the Court of Wards was retaining the possession of the mortgaged property illegally is not correct; that it is not correct that before and after acquisition of rent receiving interest the officers of the Court of Wards in collusion with designing persons leased out, sold and otherwise disposed of various moveable and immovable mortgaged properties and mis-appropriated wholly or partly the proceeds of the mortgage property, that as there is ample provision under the Court of Wards Act for adjudication of the dispute of the kind as stated in the writ petition and that the petitioners having had not resorted to that forum the writ petition so filed is not maintainable; that it has not been established by any competent Court that the petitioners as well as the said respondents are the heirs and successors of Nowab of Dhaka Khaja Salimullah Bahadur and that they are the proprietors of the estate jointly or individually; that the matter of succession to the property of the estate by the petitioners and the said respondent being a disputed question and, as such, the Court of Wards cannot release the property until the dispute is resolved or determined by a competent Civil Court, that the petitioners ought to have reported to the Court of Wards for settlement of their claim in respect of the property in the light of the provision of the Court of Wards Act; that as there is conflicting claim amongst the wards and that joint proprietorship as has not been partitioned, the Court of Wards cannot release the property in favour of the petitioners and the said respondents. 

 7. Petitioners have filed the writ petition seeking release of the property which was placed under the management of the Court of Wards on the application of Nawab of Dhaka Khaja Salimullah Bahadur and that the said property was mortgaged jointly by the Nawab and the Court of Wards to the Secretary of State for India for repayment of the debt of Taka 14 lakh of the Nawab. It is the contention of the petitioners that the mortgage was made in 1908 for a period of 30 years as security towards the payment of Taka 14 lakh and that the said amount of Taka 14 lakh since 1908 and by the time till the date of filing of the writ petition has been repaid or satisfied and, as such, the petitioners and the said respondents being the heirs and successors in interest of the Nawab are entitled to have the property released from the management of Court of Wards. Against the aforesaid contention of the petitioners and the said respondents, the respondent Nos.2 and 5 have submitted that matter as to repayment or satisfaction of the debt needs adjudication on investigation of complicated facts and that that having not been done and that also no material having been placed in the writ petition in support of the claim of the petitioners that the mortgage debt has been satisfied, as such, relief that has been sought in the writ petition cannot be had to the petitioners or, in other words, writ petition cannot be maintained by the petitioners. Respondent Nos. 2 and 5 have also contended that part of the property that was placed under the management of the Court of Wards has become abandoned property and that in the absence of determination as to how much of the property has become abandoned property, petitioners' prayer for releasing the property to them that was placed under management of the Court of Wards by the mortgage deed of the year 1908 cannot be entertained.

fulldatas.lawyer:
Mr. Zainul Abedin, Senior Advocate with Mr. Azizur Rahman Dulu, Advocate ------ For the appellant
Ms. Sharmin Hamid, A.A.G with Mr. Sultan Mahmood Banna, A.A.G ------ For the State
Mr. A.K.M. Alamgir Parvez Bhuiyan, Advocate ------ For the respondent No. 2 (ACC)
fulldatas.parties:
Mirza Saifur Rahman ------ Appellant
Vs.
The State and another ------ Respondents
fulldatas.full_judgment:
This appeal under Section 10 of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 is directed against the impugned judgment and order dated 24.06.2024 passed by Special Judge, Court No. 01, Dhaka in Special Case No. 04 of 2024 (arising out of Metropolitan Special Case No. 108 of 2019), ACCGR No. 113 of 2019 convicting the appellant under Section 161 of the Penal Code, 1860 and Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and sentencing him under Section 161 of the Penal Code, 1860 to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2(two) years and fine of Tk. 2,00,000.00 (two lakh), in default, to suffer imprisonment for 6(six) months and sentencing him under Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2(two) years and fine of Tk. 2,00,000.00 (two lacks), in default, to suffer imprisonment for 6(six) months which will run concurrently. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that the accused Mirza Saifur Rahman was the Engineer and Ship Surveyor at Sadarghat, Dhaka under the Directorate of Shipping. P.W. 4 Md. Monirujjaman Monir, Manager of M.S Shipping Lines Limited made a complaint on 01.09.2019 to the Director, Divisional Office, ACC, Dhaka stating that on 07.06.2019 the accused demanded Tk. 2,00,000 as a bribe to survey the ship MV Khadijatul Kobra which was damaged in an accident that took place on 07.06.2019. After that, the Commissioner of Anti-Corruption Commission on 01.09.2019 formed a trap team headed by P.W. 1 Md. Abdul Wadud to conduct a trap regarding the alleged demand of bribe by the accused Engineer Mirza Saifur Rahman. On 02.09.2019 at about 9.15 am P.W. 4 Md. Moniruzzaman produced 200 notes of Tk. 1000 to the ACC and a list of inventory was prepared at 9.15 am. Thereafter, the members of the trap team and P.W. 4 went to the office of the accused situated at BIWTA Bhaban, Motijheel, Dhaka and P.W. 4 entered the room of the accused and the members of the trap team remained in hiding beside the office room of the accused and different floor of the BIWTA Bhaban. After handing over the bribe amounting to Tk. 2,00,000 as mentioned in the list of inventory to the accused at about 11.40 am the members of the trap team recovered Tk. 2,00,000 from the third drawer of the accused kept in the A4 size khaki envelope. On interrogation, the accused admitted that he received the bribe amounting to Tk. 2,00,000 from P.W. 4. 

 3. P.W. 21 Md. Monirul Islam, Assistant Director, Anti-Corruption Commission, Combined District Office, Dhaka-1 was appointed as Investigating Officer vide memo dated 03.09.2019. During the investigation, he visited the place of occurrence, prepared the sketch map and index, recorded the statement of witnesses under Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, seized documents and prepared the seizure list. He found the prima facie truth of the allegation made against the accused in the FIR. After completing the investigation, submitted the memo of evidence against the accused and obtained approval on 18.11.2019 from the Anti-Corruption Commission, Head Office, Dhaka and submitted charge sheet on 25.11.2019 against the accused under Section 161 of the Penal Code, 1860 and Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 4. After that, the case record was sent to the Senior Special Judge, Dhaka who by order dated 05.02.2020 took cognizance of the offence against the accused under Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and sent the case to the Special Judge, Court No. 8, Dhaka who framed charge against the accused under Section 161 of the Penal Code, 1860 and Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 which was read over and explained to him and he pleaded not guilty to the charge and claimed to be tried following the law. Subsequently, the Divisional Special Judge, Dhaka by order dated 02.09.2021 passed in Metropolitan Criminal Transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 49 of 2021 sent the case to the Special Judge, Court No. 3, Dhaka. After that, the case was again transferred to the Special Judge, Court No. 1, Dhaka. The prosecution examined 21(twenty-one) witnesses to prove the charge against the accused and the defense cross-examined the prosecution witnesses. After examination of the prosecution witnesses, the accused was examined under Section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 and the defense examined 3(three) D.Ws. After concluding the trial, the trial Court by impugned judgment and order convicted the accused and sentenced him as stated above against which he filed the instant appeal. 

 5. P.W. 1 Md. Abdul Wadud was the Assistant Director, Combined District Office, ACC, Dhaka. He stated that while he was discharging his duty in the said post, one Monirujjaman, Manager of MS Shipping Lines, applied on 01.09.2019 to the Director, Divisional Office, ACC, Dhaka stating that a ship named Khadijatul Kobra was damaged on 07.06.2019 in an accident at Narayanganj area with এমভি বাবা মায়ের দোয়া, sand carrying ball gate. As Manager of the MS Shipping Lines, he requested the accused Engineer Mirza Saifur Rahman to survey the damaged ship and the accused advised him to file an online application and demanded Tk. 03 lakh as bribe. He also stated that unless the bribe is paid, he will not survey the ship. Finally, he demanded Tk. 02 lakh to survey the ship. On 23.06.2019 the complainant Monirujjaman paid the survey fee, income tax and conservancy fee. On 24.06.2019 he produced the dock certificate and online application. On perusal of the evidence, it appears that P.W. 4 applied on 01.09.2019 (exhibit 1) to the Director, Anti-Corruption Commission, Divisional Office, Dhaka stating that on 01.09.2019 the accused Mirza Saifur Rahman demanded bribe amounting to Tk. 2 lacks to survey the ship M.V. Khadijatul Kobra damaged in an accident took place on 07.06.2019 at Narayanganj area. Thereafter, AFM Aminul Islam, Commissioner of Anti-Corruption Commission, Divisional Office, Dhaka by office order dated 01.09.2019 (exhibit 2) formed a 13- member trap team headed by P.W. 1 Md. Abdul Wadud, Assistant Director, ACC, Combined District Office, Dhaka-1 and P.Ws 10 to 19 and 21 were the members of the trap team. Md. Kamruzzaman, Sub-Assistant Director, ACC, Combined District Office, Dhaka-2 was another member of the trap team. Amongst those members, P.Ws. 11 to 17 and 21 were the Officers of the ACC and P.Ws. 10, 18 and 19 were the police personnel. Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 empowers the Commissioner of the Anti-Corruption Commission to form a trap team headed by an officer of the said commission. In Rule 16 of the said Rules no provision is made to include any police personnel in the trap team to conduct the trap. Therefore, I am of the view that P.Ws. 10, 18 and 19 were included as members of the trap team in violation of Rule 16 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007.

 47. P.W. 3 Zunayed Arefin Bhuiyan, Sub-Divisional Engineer of Public Works Department-5, Sher-E-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka and P.W. 5 Md. Abdul Awal, Assistant Commissioner and Executive Magistrate of the Office of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka were allegedly present at the time of preparing the list of inventory and the trap proceeding. P.W. 1 stated that P.Ws. 3 and 5 were appointed by the concerned authority on the requisition of the ACC. No requisition of the ACC as to the appointment of P.Ws. 3 and 5 and the letter of appointment of P.Ws. 3 and 5 by the concerned authority regarding their presence at the time of preparing the list of inventory and conducting the trap was proved by the prosecution. In the absence of any requisition and appointment of P.Ws 3 and 5, it cannot be said that P.Ws. 3 and 5 were appointed by their authority to present at the time of preparing the list of inventory and conducting the trap. It is found that from the time of handing over 200 currency notes of Tk. 1000 by P.W. 4 to ACC till the alleged recovery of money, P.Ws 3 and 5 were with the trap party. 

 48. P.W.5 Md. Abdul Awal was the Assistant Commissioner and Executive Magistrate, Dhaka. In Rule 16 of the Anti-corruption Commission Rules, 2007 nothing has been mentioned as regards the presence of a Magistrate during conducting a trap. A Magistrate discharges judicial duty and delivers judgment considering the evidence adduced by the parties. If a Magistrate is allowed to join the trap team of ACC, it will undermine the prestige and dignity of a Magistrate. It is regrettable that in a trap arranged by the ACC, the Magistrate was involved along with the trap party from beginning to end.

During cross-examination, he stated that possibly on the 3rd or 4th of June, 2019 he went to Jashore and on 27.06.2019 he came back to Dhaka. In reply to a question, he affirmed that since he was not present in Dhaka, he was not aware of who looked after the work regarding the survey of the ship from 04.06.2019 to 27.06.2019. He is also not aware of who went to the surveyor on 07.06.2019. P.W. 7 Zahangir Hossain is the owner of the ship M.V. Khadijatul Kobra. He stated that he filed an online application on 24.06.2019 for a survey of the ship and he sent the Manager to Sadarghat, BIWTA Office. 

 53. On scrutiny of the evidence of P.Ws. 4 and 7, it appears that the evidence of P.Ws. 4 and 7 regarding filing an online application on 24.06.2019 by them is contradictory. It is found that no online application regarding repairing the said ship allegedly damaged in an accident that took place on 7.6.2019 was proved in the case. P.W. 7 stated that no agreement between the Sattarkhan Dockyard and M.S. Shipping Lines was executed regarding the repairing of the ship. The bills for repairing the ship were not handed over to the Investigating Officer. From 04.06.2019 to 27.06.2019, he was present at Satkhira. During cross-examination, he stated that he could not remember where he communicated with the accused from 07.06.2019 to 2.09.2019. In the application dated 01.09.2019 (exhibit 1), it has been alleged that on 01.09.2019 at 10.30 am, P.W. 4 went to the office of the accused allegedly situated on the 7th floor, BIWTA Bhaban, Motijheel, Dhaka. From office order dated 18.08.2019 (Annexure-G) issued by the Directorate of the Inland Shipping, reveals that at the time of the alleged occurrence on 01.09.2019 and 02.09.2019, the accused Mirza Saifur Rahman was posted as Engineer and Ship Surveyor at Sadarghat. 

 54. During cross-examination, P.W. 7 Zahangir Hossain, owner of the ship MV Khadijatul Kobra, affirmed that from 04.06.2019 to 27.06.2019 he was not present in Dhaka and he is aware of the work done by Manager Md. Moniruzzaman in the Satter Khan Dockyard from 08.06.2019 to 15.06.2019. From 04.06.2019 to 27.06.2019 he was not present in the Keraniganj area. He affirmed that from 04.06.2019 to 27.06.2019 he was present at Satkhira. PW.4 Md. Moniruzzaman stated that at the time of docking the ship, he was sick at Khulna. After two months of filing an online application, he came to know about the online application. Evidence of P.Ws 4 and 7 as regards repairing M.V. Khadijatul Kobra from 11.06.2019 to 15.06.2019 in the Sattar Khan Dockyard is contradictory. 

 55. No documentary evidence was adduced by the prosecution to prove that the accused Mirza Saifur Rahman was posted in the office of BIWTA Bhaban, Motijheel Dhaka. During cross-examination, P.W. 21 affirmed that he did not find any document from the authority of the accused to prove that the office of the accused was situated at Motijheel. He did not find any document regarding discharging the additional duty of the accused. P.W. 12 admitted that there was no nameplate outside the office room (Motijheel) of the accused. The Office order dated 18.08.2019 issued by the DG, Directorate, Inland Shiping (exhibit ‘G’) proved that the office of the accused Mirza Saifur Rahman was situated at Sadarghat. I am of the view that at the time of occurrence on 02.09.2019 the Office of the accused Mirza Saifur Rahman was situated only at the River Port, Sadarghat. The evidence of P.Ws. 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 10 to 19 and 21 that on 02.09.2019 at 10.30 am, they went to the Office of the accused situated at BIWTA Bhaban, Motijheel, Dhaka and P.W. 4 handed over Tk. 2 lakh at 11.40 am to the accused Mirza Saifur Rahman as bribe finds no substance. 

 56. In a trap case, the prosecution is required to prove that an official act was pending to the delinquent officer and he received the bribe to discharge the official act. The defense examined 3(three) witnesses in the case. The defense case is that on 02.09.2019 when the accused Mirza Saifur Rahman was going to his Office at Sadarghat at about 8.00 am at the instance of S.M. Nazmul Haque, Engineer and Ship Surveyor of the BIWTA, he was abducted along with D.W. 3 Khan Mafizul Islam by the people of the Anti-Corruption Commission with the help of the police personnel. The accused Mirza Saifur Rahman was examined as D.W. 1. He stated that on 07.06.2019, he was not present at Sadarghat and it was Friday and a government holiday. He proved the attendance register as exhibit E1 and the office order dated 18.08.2019 as exhibit G which proved that 07.06.2019 was a holiday and from 18.08.2019 to 30.08.2019 accused Mirza Saifur Rahman, Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Sadarghat was on official duty in China and at that time, Mohammad Ahoteshamul Haque Fakir discharged duty as Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Dhaka. 

 57. D.W. 1 accused Mirza Saifur Rahman stated that on 02.09.2019 he was abducted by 6/7 unknown persons from the Bijoynagar Water Tank area, Dhaka and taken to ACC Combined District Office, Dhaka- 1 at 8.45 am by a microbus. D.W. 3 Khan Mafizul Islam was cited as a witness in the charge sheet. He stated that on 02.09.2019 at 8.00 am he was waiting standing on Bijoynagar Shahid Syed Nazrul Islam Sarani and at 8.15 am he saw that 6/7 persons encircled a rickshaw and he heard the hue and cry “আমাকে ফোন করতে দেন, আমাকে ধরছেন কেন?” At that time, he found Engineer Mirza Saifur Rahman and he was abducted along with Mirza Saifur Rahman and at 8.45 am they were taken to the Office of the ACC, Segun Bagicha. He denied the suggestion that on 02.09.2019, he went to the Office of the DG Shipping Line, Motijheel. By cross-examining, the defense failed to assail the evidence of D.W. 3 that on 02.09.2019 at about 8.00 am, he was abducted along with accused Mirza Saifur Rahman from Bijoynagar Area and was taken to the Office of the ACC, Combined District Office, Dhaka. By cross-examining D.W. 1 and 3, the defense affirmed that D.W. 1 was abducted on 02.09.2019 at about 8.00 am along with D.W. 3 which disproved the evidence of P.Ws. 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 10 to 19 and 21 that on 02.09.2019 at about 11.40 am the accused Mirza Saifur Rahman received Tk. 2,00,000 as bribe from P.W. 4 Md. Monirujjaman Monir. 

 58. D.W. 2 Md. Mahmudul Hasan is the Inspector, Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Narayanganj. He stated that on 21.01.2018 he was transferred as Inspector to the Dhaka River Port, Sadarghat and he was transferred from that post on 17.07.2022 to Narayanganj. He proved the office order dated 08.10.2018 as exhibit H. He stated that the hardcopy of the online application for the survey of the ship M.V. Khadijatul Kobra was not submitted to him for which he couldn't verify whether any online application regarding the survey of the said ship was submitted or not. He affirmed that from 21.01.2018 to 17.07.2022 he discharged his duty under the accused Mirza Saifur Rahman and the accused was his immediate higher officer. The evidence of D.W. 2 that hardcopy of the online application for the survey of the ship M.V. Khadijatul Kobra was not submitted to him is not denied by the prosecution. It is already found that the prosecution failed to prove any casualty of the ship M.V. Khadijatul Kobra allegedly took place on 07.06.2019 and no evidence regarding the repairing of the said ship was proved. The prosecution also failed to prove any hardcopy or online application regarding the survey of the said ship allegedly damaged in a casualty that took place on 07.06.2019. Therefore, I am of the view that no official act was pending to the accused Mirza Saifur Rahman on 02.09.2019 to be discharged by him regarding the alleged survey of the M.V. Khadijatul Kobra.
